Ilsinho (born 12 October 1985) is a Brazilian football player. He plays for Shakhtar Donetsk. Ukrainian Premier League: 2007–08, 2009–10, 2011–12, 2012–13, 2013–14 Summer Olympics Bronze medal winner: 2008 Best XI Ukrainian Premier League: 2007–2008

Ilona Novák (May 16, 1925 – March 14, 2019) was a Hungarian swimmer and Olympic champion. She competed at the 1948 Olympic Games in London, where she finished 4th in 100 m backstroke and 5th in 4 × 100 m freestyle relay. At the 1952 Olympic Games in Helsinki she received a gold medal in 4 × 100 m freestyle relay as captain of the Hungarian team. She was added into the International Swimming Hall of Fame in Fort Lauderdale, Florida in 1973. She was born in Budapest and died on March 14, 2019 in Budapest, aged 93.

Ilona Yudina (28 June 1984 - 21 May 2018) is a Ukrainian female Paralympic sitting volleyball player. She was part of the Ukrainian women's national sitting volleyball team. She competed at the 2004 Summer Paralympics, 2008 Summer Paralympics, 2012 Summer Paralympics winning the bronze medal, 2016 Summer Paralympics, 2010 World Championships, and 2014 World Championships.

Ilse Arts (born 7 June 1990) is a Dutch wheelchair basketball player. She won a gold medal at the 2020 Summer Paralympics, gold medal at the 2018 world championships and multiple gold medals at the European Championships (2017, 2019, 2021) She won a bronze medal at the 2016 Summer Paralympics. She played at the 2017 Women's Wheelchair Basketball European Championship and 2018 Wheelchair Basketball World Championship (World Champions). She is from Wijchen, Netherlands. She played association football for SC Woezik. She was injured after a motorcycle accident. She currently plays for BBC Münsterland in the 1. Rollstuhlbasketball-Bundesliga, she transferred from the Hot Rolling Bears Essen in the 2. Rollstuhlbasketball-Bundesliga.

Ilse Pluimers (born 29 April 2002) is a Dutch professional racing cyclist from Enter, who currently rides since 2021 for UCI Women's Continental Team AG Insurance–NXTG. She competed at the 2022 Tour de France Femmes. Her brother is cyclist Rick Pluimers and her grandfather Johan Pluimers was also a cyclist.

Ilya Kharun (born February 7, 2005) is a Canadian swimmer. He has competed in the 4×50 m mixed medley, 100 m butterfly, and 10 m platform events. Kharun was born in Montreal to his mother and father who were both Cirque du Soleil performers. Kharun would first compete professionally for the Canadian national team at the 2022 World Short Course championships. At the event, he would win a silver medal in the 100 m butterfly event and a bronze medal in the 4×50 m mixed medley event with his partners Kylie Masse, Javier Acevedo, Maggie Mac Neil, Ingrid Wilm, and Rebecca Smith. Kharun made his Olympics debut at the 2020 Summer Olympics. At the games, he competed in the 200 m butterfly event and he would go on to win the bronze medal. This was the first time a Canadian man had medaled in the 200-metre butterfly event. He would also compete in the 100 m event and win another bronze medal.

Ilse Drieling (born 29 April 1909) was a German track and field athlete, specialized in the sprint events but also competed in other events. She was active during the 1920s and early 1930s, during the early era of women’s athletics in Germany. In the 4 x 100 meters relay she was the world record holder and national champion. She was a member of SV Victoria 96 Magdeburg and represented Germany at international competitions. Drieling was born on 29 April 1909. She had a twin sister Rose Drieling who was also an athletics competitor. She was specialized as a sprinter (100 meter, 200 meter, 4 x 100 meter relay) and also competed in the long jump, shot put, javelin throw and from 1932 also in the pentathlon. Together with SC Magdeburg teammates Anneliese Jacke, Lieselotte Hellmann and her sister Rose Drieling she set an official world record in the 4 × 100 meter relay in Breslau on 7 August 1927 during the with a time of 50.0 seconds. The team also became national champion in 1927 with a time of 49.8 seconds. The team was runner-up during the national championships in 1926 and 1928. In 1930, the relay team finished in third place, with Erika Kreplin running instead of Jacke. Drieling represented Germany for the first time at the 1928 Great Britain–Germany–France women's athletics match. She won with the German team the 4 x 100 meters relay and finished second in the 200 meters behind Daisy Ridgley. She also competed at the where she finished second in the 4 x 100 meters relay and third in the 100 meter.

Ilya Valeryevich Kovalchuk (; born 15 April 1983) is a Russian former professional ice hockey left winger. He played parts of 14 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Atlanta Thrashers, New Jersey Devils, Los Angeles Kings, Montreal Canadiens, and Washington Capitals. Outside the NHL, Kovalchuk played for Ak Bars Kazan and Khimik Moscow Oblast of the Russian Superleague (RSL), as well as, Spartak Moscow, SKA Saint Petersburg, and Avangard Omsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He is a three-time Gagarin Cup champion, winning with SKA in 2015 and 2017, and with Avangard in 2021. Kovalchuk is also both a three-time KHL and NHL All-Star, being named to the NHL ones in 2004, 2008, and 2009. He won the Maurice "Rocket" Richard Trophy in 2004, sharing the trophy with Rick Nash and Jarome Iginla. Internationally, Kovalchuk played for both Russia and the Olympic Athletes from Russia team. He won a bronze medal with Russia at the 2002 Winter Olympics and won a gold medal with the OAR team with them at the 2018 Winter Olympics. Before playing in the NHL, Kovalchuk played parts of two seasons with Spartak Moscow of the Vysshaya Liga. He was drafted 1st overall by the Atlanta Thrashers in the 2001 NHL entry draft. With this pick, Kovalchuk became the first Russian to ever be drafted 1st overall in the NHL. On 14 August, Kovalchuk signed an entry-level contract to join the Thrashers. On 4 October, Kovalchuk made his NHL debut in a 2–1 win against the Buffalo Sabres. During the game, he also recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Niklas Hagman goal. Two days later, he scored his first career NHL goal against Byron Dafoe in a 4–3 overtime loss against the Boston Bruins. Kovalchuk was productive in his rookie season, scoring 29 goals and recording 22 for 51 points. He was second in voting begins his teammate Dany Heatley for the Calder Memorial Trophy but was named to the NHL All-Rookie Team. He had a successful 2003–04 season, scoring 41 goals and recording 46 assists for 87 points. He was awarded the Maurice "Rocket" Richard Trophy that season, which he shared with Rick Nash and Jarome Iginla. He was selected for his first NHL All-Star game that season. After the NHL entered a lockout, Kovalchuk decided to head back to Russia and play for Ak Bars Kazan and Khimik Moscow Oblast of the Russian Superleague (RSL). After the lockout ended, Kovalchuk intended to come back to the NHL and play for the Thrashers but he was unable to agree to a new contract with the team and stayed in Russia to continue playing for Khimik Moscow Oblast. On 8 October 2005, Kovalchuk signed a five-year, $32 million contract to stay with the Thrashers. During the 2006–07 season, Kovalchuk was able to help the Thrashers reach their first-ever playoffs. The Thrashers went on to be defeated by the New York Rangers four games to zero in the first round. It was the first and last time in the Thrashers history that they reached the playoffs. On 11 January 2009, the Thrashers named Kovalchuk as the next captain of the team. The Thrashers first attempted to re-sign Kovalchuk to a twelve-year, $101 million contract and then a seven-year, $70 million contract but he declined both offers. On 4 February 2010, the Thrashers traded Kovalchuk along with Anssi Salmela and a 2010 second-round draft pick to the New Jersey Devils in exchange for Niclas Bergfors, Patrice Cormier, Johnny Oduya, and both a 2010 first- and second round draft pick. He helped the Devils during the playoffs. They defeated the Florida Panthers, Philadelphia Flyers, and the New York Rangers. They eventually went on to be defeated the Los Angeles Kings four games to two in the Final. Kovalchuk was playing injured during the playoffs after he herniated a disc in his lower back. On 1 July 2010, Kovalchuk became an unrestricted free agent. There were many offers for him during this time. On 19 July, Kovalchuk decided to agree on a seventeen-year, $102 million contract to remain with the Devils. It was the largest contract ever in NHL history. The NHL did not like this deal because it was used to get around the salary cap and they decided to block it. On 4 September, the NHL approved the next submitted deal and Kovalchuk signed a fifteen-year, $100 million contract to stay with the Devils. After the NHL went into another lockout, Kovalchuk returned to Russia and played for SKA Saint Petersburg of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He did not return to the Devils immediately after the lockout ended. Instead, he decided to play in the KHL All-Star game. On 11 July 2013, Kovalchuk announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey in the NHL. Four days later on 15 July, Kovalchuk signed a four-year contract to re-join SKA Saint Petersburg. He helped SKA during the playoffs. They defeated Torpedo Nizhny Novgorod, Dynamo Moscow, and CSKA Moscow. They eventually went on to defeat Ak Bars Kazan four games to one in the Final to win the Gagarin Cup. Kovalchuk won the playoffs MVP but refuses to accept it and gave the award to his teammate Evgenii Dadonov. On 23 June 2018, Kovalchuk decided to come out of retirement and returned to the NHL after signing a three-year, $6.25 million contract to join the Los Angeles Kings. On 5 February 2019, Kovalchuk and the Kings played against the Devils. It was Kovalchuk's first time back in New Jersey and every time he touched he puck, he was booed by angry Devils fans who felt that he abandoned the team. The Kings went on to defeat the Devils 5–1. On 17 December 2019, the Kings put Kovalchuk on unconditional waivers and he cleared them to become a free agent. On 3 January 2020, Kovalchuk signed a one-year, two-way contract to join the Montreal Canadiens. He played 22 games for the Canadiens, scoring 6 goals and recording 7 assists for 13 points. On 23 February 2020, the Canadiens traded Kovalchuk to the Washington Capitals in exchange for a 2020 third-round pick. He played 22 games for the Capitals, scoring 1 regular season goal and recording 3 assists for 4 points. on 26 December 202, Kovalchuk once again left the NHL and returned to the KHL after signing a two-year contract to join Avangard Omsk. He helped Avangard during the playoffs. They defeated Avtomobilist Yekaterinburg, Metallurg Magnitogorsk, and Ak Bars Kazan. They eventually went on to defeat CSKA Moscow four games to two in the Final to win his second Gagarin Cup. On 14 March 2025, Kovalchuk announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey.

Ilya Andreyevich Mikheyev (; born 10 October 1994) is a Russian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Toronto Maple Leafs and Vancouver Canucks. Outside of the NHL, Mikheyev played for Avangard Omsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, Mikheyev played four seasons with Avangard Omsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He had a successful time with Avangard. He helped them when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated Ak Bars Kazan, Barys Astana, and Salavat Yulaev Ufa. They were eventually defeated by CSKA Moscow four games to zero in the Finals. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On 6 May 2019, Mikheyev decided to head to North America and signed a one-year, $925,000 entry-level contract to join the Toronto Maple Leafs of the National Hockey League (NHL). On 2 October 2019, Mikheyev made his NHL debut in a 5–3 win against the Ottawa Senators. During the game, he scored his first NHL goal against Craig Anderson. On 20 October 2020, Mikheyev signed a two-year, $3.29 million contract to stay with the Leafs. On 13 July 2022, Mikheyev signed a four-year, $19 million contract to join the Vancouver Canucks. He was forced to miss most of pre-season and three regular season games after he tore his anterior cruciate ligament. He played parts of two seasons with the Canucks. On 26 June 2024, the Canucks traded Mikheyev along with Sam Lafferty and a 2027 second-round draft pick back to the Chicago Blackhawks in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick.

Ilya Nikolaevich Lyubushkin (; born 6 April 1994) is a Russian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Arizona Coyotes, Toronto Maple Leafs, Buffalo Sabres, Anaheim Ducks, and Dallas Stars. Outside of the NHL, Lyubushkin played for Lokomotiv Yaroslavl of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, Lyubushkin played five seasons with Lokomotiv Yaroslavl of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He was not drafted by an NHL team. On 14 June 2019, Lyubushkin signed a one-year entry-level contract to join the Arizona Coyotes of the National Hockey League (NHL). On 6 October 2018, Lyubushkin made his NHL debut in a 1–0 loss against the Anaheim Ducks. On 22 December 2018, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Conor Garland goal in a 6–4 win against the Colorado Avalanche. On 7 April 2021, Lyubushkin scored his first NHL goal against Jonathan Quick in a 4–3 loss against the Los Angeles Kings. On 19 February 2022, the Coyotes traded Lyubushkin along with Ryan Dzingel to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for Nick Ritchie and a 2025 conditional second-round draft pick. On 2 May, he made his playoff debut and fought Tampa Bay Lightning player Corey Perry during the game. He scored 2 goals and recorded 4 assists in 31 regular season games and recorded 1 assist in 7 playoff games for the Leafs. On 13 July 2022, Lyubushkin signed a two-year, $5.5 million contract to join with the Buffalo Sabres. On 23 February 2023, Lyubushkin scored his first goal with the Sabres. It was a short-handed goal on a breakaway and was also the overtime winner. It was the first overtime shorthanded winning goal in Sabres franchise history. On 18 August 2023, the Sabres traded Lyubushkin to the Anaheim Ducks in exchange for a 2025 fourth-round draft pick. He recorded 4 assists in 55 regular season games for the Ducks. On 29 February 2024, Lyubushkin was involved in a three-team trade. The Ducks traded him back to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for a 2025 third-round draft pick. The Carolina Hurricanes were also involved in the trade and received the Leaf's 2024 sixth-round draft pick while trading the rights to Kirill Slepets to the Leafs. He recorded 4 assists in 19 regular season games and recorded 3 assists in 7 playoff games in his return with the Leafs. On 1 July 2024, Lyubushkin signed a three-year, $9.75 million contract to join the Dallas Stars. He played parts of two seasons with the Stars. On 18 August 2023, the Stars traded Lyubushkin along with Mavrik Bourque to the Nashville Predators in exchange for a 2027 second-round draft pick and a 2028 third-round draft pick.

Ilya Protas (,; born July 18, 2006) is a Belarusian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Hershey Bears of the American Hockey League (AHL) and is under contract as a prospect for the Washington Capitals of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Protas played one season with Des Moines Buccaneers of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and one season with the Windsor Spitfires of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a succesasful time with his teams. With the Buccaneers, he was named to the USHL All-Rookie Team. With the Spitfires, he won the William Hanley Trophy as the OHL's most sportsmanlike player and was named to the All-Star Second team. He was drafted 75th overall by the Washington Capitals in the 2024 NHL entry draft. On 6 July 2024, Protas signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Capitals. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Hershey Bears. On 8 April 2026, the Capitals called him up and Protas made his NHL debut in a 4–0 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs. During the third period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Cole Hutson goal. On 11 April, Protas scored his first NHL goal against Artūrs Šilovs and also assisted on two goals in a 6–3 win against the Pittsburgh Penguins. Protas's older brother, Aliaksei, is also a professional ice hockey player.

Syed Imad Wasim Haider (in Punjabi and ) commonly known as Imad Wasim born on December 18, 1988, in Swansea, Wales, is a former Pakistani cricketer known for his left-arm spin bowling and handy batting skills. Although born in Wales, he represented Pakistan in 55 ODIs and 66 T20Is. He was the member of the Pakistan team that won the 2017 ICC Champions Trophy. He was also included in the squad in the 2019 World Cup and the 2021 T20 World Cup. On 24 November, 2023, Imad announced his retirement from all formats of international cricket. Imad Wasim was born in Swansea, Wales. His dad worked as an engineer in the UK for a short time. When Imad was very young, his family moved to Pakistan. He grew up there and started playing cricket. Before becoming a cricketer, he was studying to become a doctor. But when he got the opportunity to play for Pakistan's under-19 team, he left his studies to focus on cricket. On 24 August 2019, Imad married Sannia Ashfaq at the Faisal Mosque in Islamabad. On 4 March 2021, the couple were blessed with a daughter who they named Inaya.

Ilya Ivanovich Solovyov (; born 20 July 2000) is a Belarusian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Pittsburgh Penguins of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Calgary Flames and Colorado Avalanche. Outside of the NHL, Solovyov played for Dinamo Minsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, Solovyov played one season with the Saginaw Spirit of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL) and one season with Dinamo Minsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He was drafted 205th overall by the Calgary Flames in the 2020 NHL entry draft. On 6 April 2021, Solovyov signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Flames. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Stockton Heat and Calgary Wranglers. On 26 October 2023, the Flames called him up and Solovyov made his NHL debut in a 3–0 loss against the St. Louis Blues. On 5 December 2023, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Connor Zary goal in a 5–2 loss against the Minnesota Wild. On 18 September 2024, Solovyov signed a two-year, $775,000 contract to stay with the Flames. On 2 October 2025, the Flames placed Solovyov onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Colorado Avalanche the next day. On 10 January 2026, Solovyov scored his first NHL goal against Elvis Merzļikins in a 4–0 win against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On 20 January 2026, the Avalanche traded Solovyov to the Pittsburgh Penguins in exchange for Valtteri Puustinen and a 2026 seventh-round draft pick.

Imane Khelif is an Algerian professional boxer. Khelif has won the women’s welterweight medal at the 2024 Summer Olympics. Following wins at a series of regional victories, Khelif secured a silver medal at the 2022 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships and gold at the 2024 Olympics. Khelif was disqualified from the 2023 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships after allegedly failing unspecified sex verification tests, a decision that the International Olympic Committee (IOC) subsequently criticised as "sudden and arbitrary". In 2023, Umar Kremlev, president of the IBA, claimed that the disqualifications were because DNA tests "proved they had XY chromosomes". No public medical evidence exists that Khelif is transgender. Imane Khelif’s trainer has said that Khelif is deemed too dangerous to practice with women and was injuring many women. An endocrinologist supported "that Imane is indeed a woman, despite her karyotype and her testosterone level." The IBA was stripped from the Olympics and boxers only had to show their passport to compete. Since the introduction of mandatory sex verification testing for women by World Boxing in May 2025, Khelif has not taken part in events run by the organisation. In a February 2026 interview with CNN, Khelif revealed having high levels of testosterone. Khelif also revealed having had 'hormone treatments' for XY chromosomes before Paris Olympics, but denies being transgender. Khelif said in the interview, "I lowered my testosterone level to zero". The Algerian also has the SRY gene, often found in the Y chromosome and correlated with males. Khelif reinstated being a biological woman.

Imerio Massignan (January 2, 1937 – May 3, 2024) was an Italian professional cyclist. He was born in Altavilla Vicentina. His first professional race was the Giro d'Italia in 1959. He finished 5th overall. He did well in the Giro d'Italia for six years. His best finish was 2nd overall in 1962. At the Tour de France he won the Polka dot jersey for best climber in 1960 and 1961. In 1961 he also finished 4th overall. Later in 1961 he came second in the Giro di Lombardia. Massignan retired in 1969. He died in Novi Ligure, Italy on 3 May 2024, at the age of 87.

Imke Courtois (born 14 March 1988) is a Belgian footballer who plays as a midfielder for Standard Fémina de Liège and the Belgium women's national football team. Imke is often asked if she is Thibaut Courtois' sister. As a joke she started a company called 'Niet de zus van' and said: "for once and for all: no, Thibaut is not my brother."
Imilsis Téllez is a volleyball player from Cuba. Imilsis competed at the 1976 Summer Olympics and the 1980 Summer Olympics. She was born on 7 June 1959.

Imke de Jong (1932 – 24 January 2025) was a Dutch footballer player who played as a defender. He played with Heerenveen from 1950 to 1954 and became. He was also a professional football referee. De Jong was born in 1932. He made his debut for Heerenveen in 1950 at the age of 18. The team competed at the, the former highest football competition in the north of the Netherlands, and became champion with the team in 1951. He played on the team with among others the iconic Abe Lenstra. In 1954 De Jong left the team and moved to Zwolle to become a police officer there. He wanted to play as a semi-professional footballer at PEC Zwolle, but however the police commissioner did not allow that. He played with amateur club and later. He also became a football referee. He was for two seasons referee at the Dutch highest professional level. De Jong died on 24 January 2025, at the age of 92.

Imran Ahmed Khan Niazi (born 5 October 1952) is a Pakistani politician, cricketer, and philanthropist. He was the 22nd Prime Minister of Pakistan from 2018 to 2022 and was Member of the National Assembly of Pakistan (MNA) for three non-consecutive terms, from 2002 to 2007 and again from 2013 to 21 October 2022. He was Founder and Chairman of the Political Party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf from 1996 to 2023. Khan was born in Lahore and went to Aitchison College. He began having a skill for cricket in his school years. He started his cricket career in 1968 and played for international cricket for two decades in the late 20th century. He became captain for the Pakistan team in 1982, and led the victory in the 1992 World Cup. He created the Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital in 1994 as part of his philanthropy. He entered politics in 1996 by creating the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf and was elected Prime Minister of Pakistan in 2018. As Prime Minister, he handled COVID-1 9 in Pakistan and launched welfare programs. He was removed from office in 2022. After being Prime Minister, he survived an assassination attempt, was arrested in 2023, and has been kept in prison on several charges. He was born in Lahore on 5 October 1952. but some reports say he was born on 25 November 1952, and he has said that this is a mistake from his passport. He had four sisters and no brothers. His father was Ikramullah Khan Niazi, a civil engineer, and his mother was Shaukat Khanum. Khan was a quiet and shy boy when he was young, and grew up with his sisters in an upper middle-class situation. He went to school at the Aitchison College and Cathedral School in Lahore. In September 1971, Khan went to the Royal Grammar School Worcester in England, where he was skilled at cricket. Khan started his career as a first-class cricketer in Lahore in 1968. During his studies at the University of Oxford, he also played for their Blue's Cricket team. In 1971, he played his first international test match for Pakistan against England. In 1974, he played his first One-day international against England. He also became the second fastest all-rounder to reach the mark of 3000 runs and 300 wickets. He also has the second best batting average in test cricket at position 6. Khan became the captain of Pakistan side in 1982, becoming one of the most successful captains with 91 wins in tests and ODIs. In 1992, he led the Pakistan cricket team to victory at the world cup. His leadership as captain of the winning Pakistan team and the picture of him holding the world cup trophy for Pakistan was called “inspirational”. In 1991, he created the Shaukat Khanum Memorial Trust in memory of his mother, who died of cancer. In 1994, he built a cancer hospital called the Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital and Research Centre in Lahore to help thousands of cancer patients, it was Pakistan’s first cancer hospital. After this, he built another cancer hospital in Peshawar, and a third one in Karachi. Khan became a politician in 1996 by founding his political party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) in 1996. He supported president Pervez Musharraf from 1999. In 2007, he changed his view and then opposed Musharraf. On July 26, 2018, Khan was elected Prime Minister despite some opposition parties accusing Khan's campaign of rigging the election. Khan took oath as Prime Minister of Pakistan on 18 August 2018. As Prime Minister of Pakistan, Khan started an anti-corruption campaign and improved security. His government rebuilt minority religious sites. He also focused on education, improved health and began large welfare programs. The biggest welfare programs he launched were the Ehsaas Programme and Sehat Sahulat Program. His government also created the Zainab Alert Bill to increase the safety of women and children in Pakistan. He began the Plant for Pakistan project to help the environment. He also handled the COVID-19 Pandemic and helped revive the economy. While Khan was the prime minister, the collection of tax rose, austerity measures were taken and a worldwide economic recession due to COVID-19 happened. On April 3, 2022, he told President Arif Alvi to dissolve the National Assembly after a no-confidence motion against him failed. However, four days later on April 7, the Supreme Court later said what Khan did was illegal. A motion of no confidence was soon passed against Khan on April 10, 2022 becoming the first prime minister in Pakistan to be removed from office by a vote of no confidence. On November 3, 2022, in Wazirabad, Punjab, Khan was shot while giving a speech, but he survived the assassination attempt. On May 9, 2023 Imran Khan was arrested for alleged corruption at the High Court in Islamabad. On January 30, 2024, he was sentenced to 10 years in prison for revealing state secrets.
Imre Gedővári (1 July 1951 – 22 May 2014) was a Hungarian fencer. He won three Olympic medals in the sabre competitions. Gedővári died on 22 May 2014, following a long illness. He was 62.

Imre Földi (8 May 1938 – 23 April 2017) was a Hungarian weightlifter. Competing at a record of five Olympic Games, he won a gold medal in 1972 and silver medals in 1964 and 1968. During his career he set 21 world records, and after his retirement he coached his daughter to become a European champion. Földi earned numerous awards for his results and achievements, most notably he was named Weightlifter of the Century by the International Weightlifting Federation and was elected for Sportsperson of the Nation in Hungary.

Imre Furmen (14 August 1933 – 5 February 2021) was a Hungarian cyclist. He competed in two events at the 1952 Summer Olympics. He was born in Budapest, Hungary. Furmen died on 5 February 2021 in Budapest, aged 87.

Imran Ahmed Khan Sherwani (born 9 April 1962 died 28 November 2025) is a British former international field hockey player. He was born in Stoke-on-Trent, Staffordshire, England. Sherwani won gold with the Great Britain squad at the 1988 Summer Olympics. In June 2021, Sherwani revealed that he had been diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease.

Imrul Kayes (; born 2 February 1987) is a Bangladeshi international cricketer. He plays for Khulna Division. He is a left-hand batsman. He is also an occasional wicket-keeper. He made his first-class debut in 2006.

Inder Singh (born 23 December 1943) is an Indian former football player and captain, manager and administrator. Merdeka Tournament runner-up: 1964; third place: 1970 Santosh Trophy: 1970–71, 1974–75, 1980–81 Santosh Trophy top scorer: 1974–75 (with 23 goals; Record) Delhi Sports Journalists Association Award: 1974

Indre Sorokaite (born 2 July 1988) is an Italian volleyball player. She played at the 2013 Women's European Volleyball Championship, 2013 FIVB World Grand Prix, 2014 FIVB World Grand Prix, 2015 Montreux Volley Masters, 2015 Women's European Volleyball Championship, 2015 FIVB World Grand Prix, 2017 FIVB Volleyball World Grand Prix, 2019 FIVB Volleyball Women's Nations League, and 2019 FIVB Volleyball Women's Club World Championship. She played for Volley Bergamo and Imoco Volley Conegliano.

Indy Baijens (born 4 February 2001 in Zaandam) is a Dutch volleyball player for ASPTT Mulhouse and the Dutch national team. She participated at the 2018 FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship and 2019 FIVB Volleyball Women's Nations League.

Ineke Yperlaan-Pesman is a Dutch water polo player. She competed for the Dutch women's national water polo team in the 1986 World Aquatics Championships and 1985 European Women's Water Polo Championship.

Ines Granvorka (born 13 August 1991) is a Swiss female volleyball player. She played at the 2015 FIVB Volleyball Women's Club World Championship with her club Voléro Zürich. She played for TS Volley Düdingen.

Inesu Emiko Takeoka is a former Japanese football player. She played for the Japan national team. Takeoka was born on May 1, 1971. She played for Nikko Securities Dream Ladies. The club won Nadeshiko League championship for 3 years in a row (1996-1998). However, the club was disbanded in 1998 due to financial strain and she retired. On August 21, 1994, Takeoka debuted for the Japan national team against Austria. She was a member of Japan for 1995 World Cup. She also played at 1995 AFC Championship. She played 3 games and scored 3 goals for Japan until 1995.

Inge Joanna Francisca Vermeulen (6 January 1985 – 10 January 2015) was a Brazilian-Dutch field hockey player. She played as a goalkeeper for three teams and two international teams: Brazil and the Netherlands. Vermeulen was born in Americana, São Paulo and moved to the Netherlands at a young age. Vermeulen committed suicide (killed herself) on 10 January 2015 in Utrecht. She was 30.

Inge Huitzing (born 19 April 1974) is a Dutch wheelchair basketball player. She won a bronze medal at the 2012 Summer Paralympics, and 2016 Summer Paralympics. She played at the 2008 Summer Paralympics and 2014 Women's World Wheelchair Basketball Championship.

Bo Ingemar Erlandsson (16 November 1957 – 9 August 2022) was a Swedish footballer. He played as a defender. He represented Malmö FF between 1976 and 1987. Between 1978 and 1985, he scored two goals for the Sweden national team. Erlandsson died on 9 August 2022, at the age of 64.

Jens Ingemar "Ingo" Johansson (22 September 1932 – 30 January 2009) was a Swedish professional boxer who competed from 1952 to 1963. He held the world heavyweight title from 1959 to 1960, and was the fifth heavyweight champion born outside the United States.

Ingrid Margareta “Inga Greta” Kerstin Teodora Broman with married name Brundin (18 September 1909 - 9 December 1997) was a Swedish track and field athlete specialized in the high jump. She was a pioneer in women's sports. Her main achievement was winning the bronze medal at the 1926 Women's World Games in the high jump event. At these second Women’s World Games, she jumped 1.40 meters and lost from the French Hélène Bons with 1.50 meters and the British Hilda Hatt with 1.45 meters. Broman was born in Borås in 1909. She married metallurgist and athlete in 1937. They had two sons. She died in Ängelholm in December 1997. She is buried, together with her husband, at the Chapel Cemetery in Falkenberg.

Inger Bjørnbakken (28 December 1933 – 13 February 2021) was a Norwegian alpine skier. He was born in Bærum, Norway. She finished tied for sixth place in the women's slalom at the 1956 Winter Olympics. She also finished fourteenth in the giant slalom. Two years later, Bjørnbakken won the women's slalom at the 1958 World Championships in Bad Gastein. She later finished fourteenth in the 1960 Winter Olympics. Bjørnbakken died in a fire on 13 February 2021 at the age of 87.

Ingvar Axel Harald Ericsson (31 August 1927 – 14 May 2020) was a Swedish middle-distance runner. He was in the 1500 m event. He competed at the 1952 and 1956 Summer Olympics and finished eighth in 1952. At the European championships he was seventh in 1950 and fourth in 1954. Ericsson won the national 1500 m title in 1952, 1954 and 1955. He was a firefighter by profession.
Ingrid Stenmarck (5 February 1917 – 30 December 2011) was a Swedish swimmer. She was the Swedish national champion in the 100 metres freestyle from 1933 to 1937.

Ingrid van den Benden (born 1951) is a former Dutch Paralympic swimmer. She won three gold medals and one silver medal at the 1968 Summer Paralympics. She won four gold medals at the 1972 Summer Paralympics in Heidelberg. When Van den Bende was two, she moved with her parents from Indonesia to the Netherlands. Shortly before she arrived in the Netherlands, she had polio. For her rehabilitation she started swimming when she was four. At the time, she walked with suspenders and high shoes. During the swimming competitions of the 60th anniversary of the “Amsterdamse Specialisten Vereniging” in 1966 she swam very fast. Her performance was noticed and so she was able to compete the same year and the following year at the Stoke Mandeville Games, the annual competitions for athletes with disabilities in Great Britain. In both years she won three times. At first he trained every Thursday night at the ZAR. She was a member of the ISA swimming club in Amsterdam. She was selected to compete in the 1968 Summer Paralympics in Tel Aviv, in Israel. She has won two individual gold medals, a silver medal and a gold medal in the 3x 50m relay. After the Paralympics she was awarded in her school. It was a festive event, including a speech from the mayor. She received several gifts, including a swimming diploma: At the 1969 Dutch National Championships she swam four world records. At the 1972 Dutch National Championships she swam two world records. In the years preceding the 1972 Summer Paralympics in Heidelberg she intensified her training to a professional level, having three training sessions per day, five days a week, plus Saturday as match-day. As result she swam several long-lasting World Records and won three individual gold medals plus another gold medal as part of the 4x 100m relay.

Irving Crane (November 13, 1913 – November 17, 2001), nicknamed "the Deacon", was an American pool player from Livonia (near Rochester). He was frequent champion and leading player in the sport. He is most well known for his skill at the game of straight pool (14.1 continuous). He won six world billiards titles in this game. Crane became very interested in billiards when he was 11 years old. He started play on a toy pool table his brother received as a Christmas gift. His parents soon replaced their dining room table with a 4' by 8' pool table. Soon, Crane started to play in public at a local pool room. Crane could play all day and never get bored. He could not wait to get home from school and start to play pool. Though he taught himself to play, at age 14 he ran 89 balls in straight pool at a local pool room. He called each shot in advance. His parents replaced the smaller table with a full size tournament table. Over the next ten years some of the best players, including Willie Hoppe and Andrew Ponzi, came to practice with Crne. Despite consistent play throughout his teenage years, Crane did not enter any tournaments until he was 23 years old. In February 1939, at age 26, Crane sank 150 balls in a row against his opponent in an exhibition straight pool match. The game was played on a difficult 5' by 10' table in Layton, Utah. This was impressive. But the crowd cheered him, and he continued to play. He finally put 309 consecutive balls thus shattering the previous world record of 244 consecutive balls. He won his first world title in 1942. Over the next thirty years, Crane won almost two dozen major championships, including the World Crown in 1946, 1955, 1966, 1968, 1970 and 1972, the Ballantine International Championship in 1965, the International Roundrobin championship in 1968, and the World Series of Billiards in 1978 at age 65. At the 1966 World Crown tournament, he ran 150 and out in the finals. He never let his opponent back to the table after an early safety battle. No other player has ever done this. Crane also holds the record for the most runner-up finishes for the World Crown with 13. Crane found it hard to make a living only by playing pool, even though he was very skilled. In 1957, he began working as a Cadillac salesman at a dealership in Rochester, New York. He continued there for 17 years. At Rochester's annual auto show his dealership's exhibit had a pool table. Crane would run balls while answering questions. Working at a regular job was not Crane's first choice. In an interview with Sports Illustrated in 1969, he said "If I had to make a choice between selling cars and playing pool, I'd choose pool... The only time I've ever been really happy is when I was at a pool table." He was "tall, lean man with the imperial bearing of the headmaster of Eton," Crane got the nickname The Deacon because of his gentlemanly ways, his very cautious approach to the game and his careful style of clothing. He always wore a conservative suit when he played. The Los Angeles Times interviewed Crane's wife Althea. They were married 64 years. She said, "A lot of people, if it was a hot day and there was no air conditioning, they'd take off their coat to play. But not Irving Crane." Minnesota Fats, once said, "Irv Crane would have been the only guy to notice the horse under Lady Godiva". Willie Mosconi criticized Crane for his cautious style. He wrote in his 1993 autobiography, Willie's Game, that "Crane wouldn't take a shot unless his grandmother could make it." Crane became a member of the Billiard Congress of America's hall of fame in 1978. In 1999, Crane was number eight on Billiard Digest's fifty greatest players of the century. In 1980 Crane retired from professional play. He stopped playing entirely in about 1996. On 17 November 17 2001, four days after entering a nursing home, Crane died of natural causes. He was 88 years old.

On 8 August 2018, Lundeström signed a one-year entry-level contract to join the Ducks. On 8 October 2018, Lundeström made his NHL debut in a 3–2 shootout win against the Detroit Red Wings. On 13 October, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Kiefer Sherwood goal in a 5–3 loss against the Dallas Stars. On 6 February 2021, Lundeström scored his first NHL goal against Devan Dubnyk in a 2–1 shootout win against the San Jose Sharks. On 1 March, Lundeström recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 5–4 loss against the St. Louis Blues. On 7 August, Lundeström signed a one-year contract to stay with the Ducks. On 25 July 2022, Lundeström signed a two-year contract to stay with the Ducks. On 1 July 2025, Lundeström signed a two-year, $2.6 million contract to join the Columbus Blue Jackets.

Isao Iwabuchi was a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Iwabuchi was born in Tochigi Prefecture on November 17, 1933. He played for Keio BRB which was consisted of his alma mater Keio University players and graduates. He won 1954 and 1956 Emperor's Cup at the club. On January 5, 1955, when Iwabuchi was a Keio University student, he debuted for the Japan national team against Burma. In June 1956, at 1956 Summer Olympics qualification against South Korea, he scored a goal. After the qualification, Japan won the qualification to 1956 Summer Olympics in Melbourne by the drawing of lots. In November, he was selected Japan for 1956 Olympics. He also played at 1958 Asian Games. He played 8 games and scored 2 goals for Japan until 1958. On April 16, 2003, Iwabuchi died of peritonitis in Tokyo Metropolis at the age of 69.

Isaías "Iyo" S. Pimentel (16 February 1933 — 26 June 2017) was a Venezuelan international tennis player. He was born on the Dutch island of Curaçao. Pimentel was three times Curaçaoan champion. He competed in the Davis Cup, representing Venezuela, a number of times, from 1957 to 1966. Pimentel died on 26 June 2017 in Willemstad, Curaçao at the age of 84.

Isayah Boers (born 19 June 1999) is a Dutch sprinter. Boers represents the Netherlands at international competitions. Boers won the bronze medal at the 2022 World Athletics Indoor Championships in the 4 × 400 metres relay event. At the 2022 European Athletics Championships he finished with the relay team fourth in the 4 × 400 metres relay event.

Isak Rosén (born 15 March 2003) is a Swedish professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Winnipeg Jets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Buffalo Sabres. Outside of the NHL, Rosén has played for Leksands IF of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). Before playing in the NHL, Rosén played three seasons with Leksands IF of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). He was drafted 14th overall by the Buffalo Sabres in the 2021 NHL entry draft. On 31 May 2022, Rosén signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Sabres. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Rochester Americans. On 25 November 2023, the Sabres called him up and Rosén made his NHL debut in a 7–2 loss against the New Jersey Devils. On 27 March 2025, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Mattias Samuelsson goal in a 7–3 win against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On 1 November, Rosén scored his first NHL goal against Charlie Lindgren in a 4–3 shootout win against the Washington Capitals. On March 6, 2026, the Sabres traded Rosén along with Jacob Bryson, a 2026 conditional fourth-round draft pick, and a 2027 second-round draft pick to the Winnipeg Jets in exchange for Luke Schenn and Logan Stanley.

Ishan Pranav Kumar Pandey Kishan (born 18 July 1998) is an Indian cricketer who represents the Indian national cricket team. He is a left-handed batsman and wicket-keeper. Kishan made his international debut in 2021 and has since become a prominent player in limited-overs cricket. He plays for Jharkhand in the Ranji Trophy.
Inderbir Singh "Ish" Sodhi is a New Zealand cricketer from India. He plays for the New Zealand national cricket team. He was born on October 31, 1992.

Isiah Lord Thomas III (born April 30, 1961) is a retired American basketball player. He played professionally for the Detroit Pistons in the National Basketball Association (NBA). Thomas was just over 6 feet tall, making him a "small man" by basketball standards. He was one of the greatest point guards and players in basketball history. His only peer in the 1980s was Earvin "Magic" Johnson who played for the Los Angeles Lakers. He grew up poor on Chicago's South Side. As a boy he showed a talent for basketball. At this time Thomas realized his basketball skills might help his family get out of poverty and the unsafe neighborhood. Thomas attended the Indiana University. He was a member of the US men's basketball team at the 1980 Summer Olympics. Because of the US boycott, the team did not go to Moscow. Thomas was a first round draft choice by the Detroit Pistons. He was signed to a 4-year contract. In 1984 Thomas was given an 11-year, $12 million contract. This was both the longest and highest paying player contract in Detroit Pistons history. A torn achilles tendon forced him to retire in 1994. Thomas was the 1982 NBA Rookie of the Year. He was named the Most Valuable Player in the 1984, 1986 and 1990. He played in twelve All-star games. In 1996 he was named one of the 50 greatest players in NBA history. Thomas has one of the best records in NBA history. He scored a total of 18,822 points averaging 19.2 points per game. He was named to the NBA's 50th Anniversary All-Time Team. In 2000 he was named to the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame.

Ismail Mohamed Asif Waheed (born 13 August 1968) is an athlete from the Maldives. He ran for the Maldives in the men's 100 metres, 200 metres, and 4 × 100 metres relay at the 1988 Summer Olympics in Seoul. He did not go past the first round in any of the events.

Israel Oliver Peña (born December 16, 1987 in Madrid) is a swimmer from Spain. He has a disability: he has vision problems and is an S12/B2 type swimmer. In 2012, he lived in Carrizal de Wit, Las Palmas, Canary Islands. He raced at the 2004 Summer Paralympics. He finished second in the 4 x 100 meters 49 points medley relay. He finished third in the 100 meter Butterfly race. He raced at the 2008 Summer Paralympics. He raced at the 2012 Summer Paralympics.

Isileli "Israel" Folau (born 3 April 1989) is an Australian professional rugby player. He currently plays rugby league for French team Catalans Dragons. He also played for the Australia national rugby union team from 2013 until he was sacked in 2019. In the National Rugby League (NRL), he played for the Melbourne Storm (2007–08) and the Brisbane Broncos (2009–10). He left rugby league to play Australian rules football in the Australian Football League (AFL). He played for the Greater Western Sydney Giants from 2011 to 2012. From 2013 to 2019, he played rugby union. He played for the New South Wales Waratahs in the Super Rugby. Folau was born in Minto, New South Wales. He is of Tongan ancestry. He later moved to Queensland. He was a student at Marsden State High School with classmates Chris Sandow and Antonio Winterstein. Folau is a Christian. In the past, he has made social media posts considered by many to be anti-gay. After similar comments were posted on his Instagram in April 2019, his contract was ended by Rugby Australia.

Israel Vázquez Castañeda (December 25, 1977 – December 2, 2024) was a Mexican professional boxer who competed from 1995 to 2010. He was a three-time super bantamweight world champion. He won the IBF title from 2004 to 2005; and the WBC, The Ring titles twice from 2005 to 2008. He was born in Mexico City, Mexico. Vázquez was diagnosed with stage-4 sarcoma in November 2024. He died from the disease on December 2, 2024 at the age of 46.

Issa Hayatou (9 August 1946 – 8 August 2024) was a Cameroonian sports executive, athlete, and football administrator. He was the president of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) between 1988 and 2017. He was the acting FIFA president until 26 February 2016 after president Sepp Blatter was banned from all football-related activities in 2015. He was also a member of the International Olympic Committee (IOC). In November 2010, he was alleged by the BBC to have taken bribes in the 1990s regarding the awarding of World Cup television rights. The IOC announced it would investigate him. On 24 May 2017, he was appointed President of the National Football Academy by the President of Cameroon, Paul Biya. Hayatou died at a hospital in Neuilly-sur-Seine, France on 8 August 2024, a day before his 78th birthday.
Issey Morgan Nakajima-Farran (born 16 May 1984) is a Canadian former professional soccer player. A. Includes appearances in the UEFA Cup and CONCACAF Champions League.

Isabelle Eleanor Chih Ming Wong (15 May 2002–) is an English cricketer who was born in Chelsea, London. She is a right arm fast medium bowler who bats right-handed. In domestic cricket, Wong played for Worcestershire Women in 2018, and for Warwickshire Women since 2019. She has also played worldwide for several Twenty20 franchise teams. In international cricket, she has played for England Women since June 2022 in each of the Test, One Day International, and Twenty20 International formats.

István Bérczi (1 July 1945 – 10 April 2021) was a Hungarian gymnast. He competed in eight events at the 1972 Summer Olympics. István Bérczi died on 10 April 2021, at the age of 75, of issues related to COVID-19.

István Géczi (16 March 1944 – 10 September 2018) was a Hungarian football (soccer) goalkeeper. He played for Ferencvárosi TC. After retiring from soccer, he became a politician. István Géczi played on the Hungarian national football team during the 1972 Summer Olympics, where the Hungarian team won a silver medal. He also participated in the 1966 FIFA World Cup and UEFA Euro 1972 for the Hungary national football team. After retiring from soccer, he was a member of the Hungarian Parliament in the late 1980s. István Géczi died of a stroke in Budapest, Hungary on 10 September 2018. He was 75 years old.

István Szívós Jr. (24 April 1948 – 10 November 2019) was a Hungarian water polo player. He competed in four consecutive Olympics in 1968–1980 and won a medal in each of them. He also won six gold or silver medals at world and European championships and nine national titles. He died 10 November 2019 at the age of 71.

István Gáli (5 July 1943 – 20 February 2020) was a Hungarian boxer. He boxed as a welterweight. He won a bronze medal at the 1967 European Amateur Boxing Championships in Rome. He also competed at the 1968 Summer Olympics. Gáli was born in Bodroghalom. He died in Budapest on 20 February 2020 at the age of 76.

István Turu (25 September 1962 – February 2021) was a Hungarian boxer. He competed in the men's lightweight event at the 1988 Summer Olympics. He was born in Törökszentmiklós, Hungary. Turu died from COVID-19 during the pandemic in Hungary in February 2021, aged 58.

István Fehér (6 March 1954 – 4 March 2021) was a Hungarian wrestler. He competed in the men's freestyle 74 kg at the 1980 Summer Olympics. Fehér was born in Nagykőrös, Hungary. Fehér died in March 2021, two days before his 67th birthday.

István Szőke (13 February 1947 – 1 June 2022) was a Hungarian footballer. He played as a midfielder for Ferencvárosi TC from 1965 until 1974. He also played for the Hungary national team from 1969 until 1973, making 13 appearances. He was born in Budapest, Hungary. Szőke died on 1 June 2022 in Budapest of a stroke, aged 75.
István-Elod Tóth (born 1951) is a former Hungarian Olympian. He won the silver medal in wrestling, at the Olympic Games in Moscow, 1980. He was World Champion in 1979 and 1981.

Italo De Zan (1 July 1925 – 9 March 2020) was an Italian racing cyclist. He won the tenth Giro d'Italia in 1948. He was born in San Fior. De Zan died of COVID-19 in Treviso on 9 March 2020 at the age of 94.

Ippolito "Ito" Giani (8 September 1941 – 28 September 2018) was an Italian sprinter. He was born in Varese, Italy. From 1963 to 1967 he took part in 20 international competitions and won six medals. He was in the 1964 Summer Olympics. Giani died in Varese on 28 September 2018 at the age of 77.

Ivan Hašek (born 6 September 1963) is a former Czech football player. He played for Czechoslovakia national team and Czech Republic national team. Czechoslovak First League: 1983–84, 1984–85, 1986–87, 1987–88, 1988–89 Czechoslovak Cup: 1983–84, 1987–88, 1988–89 Czechoslovak Footballer of the Year: 1987, 1988

Ivan Boldirev (born August 15, 1949) is a Yugoslavian-born Canadian former professional ice hockey centre. He played a total of fifteen seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Boston Bruins, California Golden Seals, Chicago Black Hawks, Atlanta Flames, Vancouver Canucks, and Detroit Red Wings He led the Black Hawks in scoring during the 1977–78 and 1978–79 seasons. He was also successful during his time with the Vancouver Canucks. He would help the team reach the 1982 Stanley Cup Finals where they would lose to the New York Islanders four games to zero. After retiring, Boldirev worked with the Chicago Blackhawks Alumni Association.

Ivan Droppa (born February 1, 1972) is a Slovak retired professional ice hockey player that played 2 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL) for the Chicago Blackhawks. Droppa was drafted 37th overall in the 1990 NHL Entry Draft by the Chicago Blackhawks. Droppa mainly played in Europe during his career. He has played for the Nuremberg Ice Tigers, Kassel Huskies, and Duesseldorf EG/DEG Metro Stars of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL). The Slavia Praha HC and Litvinov CHP HC of the Czech Extraliga. The MsHK Žilina and HC Košice of the Slovak Extraliga. Droppa retired from professional ice hockey in 2010.

Pearl Iva Edith Withers (July 7, 1917 – October 7, 2014) was a Canadian-born American actress and singer. She was best known as a replacement player who had long runs in some of Rodgers and Hammerstein's biggest musical theatre hits. She also appeared in Carousel, South Pacific and Gentlemen Prefer Blondes. Withers was born in Rivers, Manitoba, Canada. Withers died in Englewood, New Jersey at age 97 on October 7, 2014 at the Lillian Booth Actors Home.

Ivan Milanov Dimitrov (; 14 May 1935 – 1 January 2019) was a Bulgarian footballer. He was born in Sofia, Bulgaria. He played as a defender for the Bulgarian national team. At club level, he made 340 appearances in the Bulgarian League, playing for Stroitel Sofia, Torpedo Sofia, Zavod 12 Sofia, Lokomotiv Sofia, Spartak Sofia and Akademik Sofia. Dimitrov died in Sofia on 1 January 2019, at the age of 83.

Ivan Duane Irwin (March 13, 1927 – February 11, 2019) was an American-born Canadian professional ice hockey defenseman. He played 155 games in the National Hockey League for the New York Rangers and Montreal Canadiens. He was born in Chicago, Illinois. Irwin was raised in Toronto, Ontario. Irwin died in Ajax, Ontario on February 11, 2019 from pneumonia, aged 91.

Ivan Vasilyevich Drago (Russian: Иван Васильевич Драго, pronounced ɪˈvan vɐˈsʲilʲjɪvʲɪdʑ ˈdraɡə) is a fictional Soviet Russian boxer from the Rocky movie series, created and played by Dolph Lundgren. He first appeared in the 1985 movie Rocky IV opposite Sylvester Stallone as the main antagonist, and in the 2018 movie Creed II as a protagonist to his son Viktor.

Ivan Havrylovich Bogdan (; February 29, 1928 – December 25, 2020) was a Ukrainian wrestler. He was born in Dmytro-Bilivka, Ukrainian SSR. He won an Olympic gold medal in 1960. He won gold medals at the 1958 and 1961 World Wrestling Championships. Bogdan died on December 25, 2020 at the age of 92.
Iurie Nicolaevici Bașcatov (20 June 1968 – 3 September 2022) was a Soviet and Moldovan freestyle swimmer. He competed at the 1988 and 1992 Summer Olympics, winning silver medals in both events.

Ivan Dmitrievich Barbashev (; born 14 December 1995) is a Russian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the St. Louis Blues. Barbashev is a two-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Blues in 2019 and the Golden Knights in 2023. Before playing in the NHL, Barbashev played parts of three seasons with the Moncton Wildcats of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He had a successful time with the Wildcats. He was named to the QMJHL All-Rookie Team. He was drafted 33rd overall by the St. Louis Blues in the 2014 NHL entry draft. On 21 July 2014, he signed a three-year, entry-level contract to join the Blues. He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Chicago Wolves. On 25 January 2017, the Blues called him up and Barbashev made his NHL debut in a 5–1 loss to the Minnesota Wild. On 7 February, Barbashev scored his first NHL goal against Andrew Hammond in a 6–0 win against the Ottawa Senators. He helped the Blues during the playoffs. They defeated the Winnipeg Jets, Dallas Stars, and San Jose Sharks. They eventually went on to defeat the Boston Bruins four games to three in the Finals to win the first Stanley Cup in Blues franchise history. On 1 September 2019, Barbashev signed a two-year, $2.95 million contract to stay with the Blues. On February 26, 2023, the Blues traded Barbashev to the Vegas Golden Knights in exchange for Zach Dean. He helped the Golden Knights during the playoffs. They defeated the Winnipeg Jets, Edmonton Oilers, and Dallas Stars. They eventually went on to defeat the Florida Panthers four games to one in the Finals to win the first Stanley Cup in Golden Knights franchise history. On 1 September 2019, Barbashev signed a five-year, $25 million contract to stay with the Golden Knights. Barbashev's older brother Sergei is also a professional ice hockey player and plays in the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL).

Ivan Alexeyevich Demidov (; born 10 December 2005) is a Russian professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Montreal Canadiens of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Demidov played for SKA Saint Petersburg of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, Demidov played 71 regular season games over three seasons with SKA Saint Petersburg of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He had as successful time with his team. He was named a two-time All-Star and was awarded the Alexei Cherepanov Award for KHL's top rookie. He was drafted 5th overall by the Montreal Canadiens in the 2024 NHL entry draft. His slection was annonunced by legendary Candian singer Celine Dion. On 8 April 2025, Demidov signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Canadiens. On 14 April 2025, Demidov made his NHL debut, recording his first NHL point after assisting on a Alex Newhook goal and then scoring his first NHL goal against Arvid Söderblom in a 4–3 shootout loss against the Chicago Blackhawks. On 1 July 2026, Demidov signed an eight-year, $73.2 million contract to stay with the Canadiens.

Ivan Ivan (born 20 August 2002) is a Czech professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Boston Bruins of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Colorado Avalanche. Before playing in the NHL, Ivan played three seasons with the Cape Breton Screaming Eagles of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He was not drafted by an NHL team. On 5 March 2024, Ivan signed a one-year entry-level contract to join the Colorado Avalanche of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Colorado Eagles. On 9 October 2024, Ivan made his NHL debut in a 8–4 loss against the Vegas Golden Knights. Three days later on 22 December 2018, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Nathan MacKinnon goal in a 6–4 loss against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On 24 October 2024, Ivan scored his first NHL goal on the powerplay against Karel Vejmelka in a 5–1 win against the Utah Hockey Club. On 27 June 2026, the Avalanche traded Ivan to the Boston Bruins in exchange for Fabian Lysell. On 29 June, Ivan signed a one-year, $850,000 contract to stay with the Bruins.

Ivan Koloff (born Oreal Perras; August 25, 1942 – February 18, 2017) was a Canadian professional wrestler. He was also called "The Russian Bear". He was best known for once holding the WWWF World Heavyweight Championship. He wrestled between 1961 and 1994. He was born in Montreal, Quebec. Koloff died from liver cancer on February 18, 2017 in Winterville, North Carolina. He was 74.

Ivo "Ivan" Mrázek (18 January 1926 – 4 April 2019) was a Czech professional basketball player and coach. He played as a point guard. In his club career, he won 6 Czechoslovak League championships (1947, 1948 2×, 1949, 1950, 1951) with Brno. He played for the Czechoslovakia national team. He won the gold medal at the EuroBasket in 1946 with the national team. He also won three EuroBasket silver medals, in 1947, 1951 and 1955. He played for Czechoslovakia in two Summer Olympics, in 1948 and 1952. Mrázek was born in Brno. He died on 4 April 2019, at the age of 93.

Ivan Kizimov (; 28 May 1928 – 22 September 2019) was a Soviet-born Russian equestrian and Olympic champion. He was born in Novocherkassk. He won a gold medal in dressage at the 1968 Summer Olympics in Mexico City, and a gold medal in team dressage at the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich.

Ivan Patzaichin (; 26 November 1949 – 5 September 2021) was a Romanian canoe racing coach and sprint canoeist. He took part in all major competitions between 1968 and 1984. He won four gold medals at the 1968, 1972, 1980 and 1984 Summer Olympics. He also won three silver medals at the 1972, 1980 and 1984 Olympics. Patzaichin was born in Crișan, Romania. Patzaichin died on 5 September 2021 in Bucharest, Romania from lung cancer, aged 71. He was diagnosed with the disease in three months before his death.

Ivan Nicholas Johnson (27 June 1953 – 4 October 2021) was a Bahamian-born English first-class cricketer and journalist. He played for Worcestershire County Cricket Club from 1972 to 1975. He was a journalist for newspapers in Fleet Street. In 1990, Johnson founded The Punch. Johnson died of a heart attack on 4 October 2021 in Nassau at the age of 68.

14 April 1947 — 19 December 2022) was a Soviet road cyclist. He was national champion and represented the Soviet Union at international races. Skosirev was born in Ust-Muta in 1947. His brother Victor Skosirev was also a cyclist who competed for the Soviet Union. Skosirev made his debut for the national team in 1971 at the Tour of Algeria where he finished second behind Polish Zbigniew Krzeszowiec. After finishing second in 1972 he won the national team time trial championship in 1973 together with Gennady Komnatov, Rinat Sharafulin and Viktor Skosyrev. In the fall of 1973, Skosyrev won the Tour of Bulgaria including a stage win. In 1974 he won the Circuit Cycliste Sarthe stage race in France ahead of Alain Meunier. Skosirev died in Omsk on 19 December 2022.

Ivan Gordon Sharpe (15 June 1889 – 9 February 1968) was an English amateur footballer. Even though he was an amateur footballer, he played for professional clubs, including Watford, Derby County, and Leeds United. He also played for the England national amateur football team and the Great Britain Olympic football team, where he won a gold medal at the 1912 Summer Olympics. After he retired, he became a sports journalist, later becoming the president of the Football Writers Association. In 1936, he was selected by the BBC to be one of two journalists (the other being Norman Creek) to provide the first ever live commentary on the FA Cup final. He continued to contribute a hard-hitting article to the Wolverhampton Wanderers match day programme for many years right up to his death. Ivan Petkov Kolev (Sofia) 1 November 1930 – 1 July 2005) was a Bulgarian footballer. He was capped 75 times for Bulgaria, and played for them at the 1962 and 1966 FIFA World Cups. He also played for Bulgaria at the 1956 Summer Olympics, where won a bronze medal. He was the first Bulgarian footballer nominated for the Ballon d'Or.

Ivan Schranz (born 13 September 1993) is a Slovak professional footballer who plays as a forward or winger for Czech First League club Slavia Prague and the Slovakia national team. Schranz finished as the joint-top scorer of the UEFA European Championship in 2024 with three goals, as his nation reached the last 16. Having started his club career in the Slovak Second League at Petržalka, where he played for a year and a half, Schranz joined Spartak Trnava at the age of 18 in January 2012. He made his league debut against Banská Bystrica on 5 May of the same year. Schranz also made his European competition debut and in July 2014 scored twice in a UEFA Europa League qualifier against Scottish Premiership club St Johnstone. In the middle of the 2014–15 season Schranz headed to Czech side Sparta Prague on loan, but made no league appearances for the side before returning to Trnava. He continued to play for Trnava until the end of the 2016–17 season, playing 125 matches and scoring 25 goals overall. On 4 September 2020, Schranz debuted for the senior Slovakia national team in a 3–1 loss against the Czech Republic at the 2020–21 UEFA Nations League, where he also scored his first goal. In May 2021, Schranz was included in Slovakia's final squad for the rescheduled UEFA Euro 2020 tournament, but did not make an appearance. In June 2024, Schranz was called up to represent Slovakia at UEFA Euro 2024. He scored the only goal of their opening match as they achieved an upset 1–0 victory over Belgium. He scored again in a 2–1 loss to Ukraine in their second match, making him the first ever Slovak player to score more than one goal at the UEFA European Championship. Schranz scored his third goal of the tournament in the round of 16 match against England. His first-half goal put Slovakia 1–0 up, a lead they held for most of the match, although England equalised in injury time and subsequently scored again in extra time for a 2–1 England win, sending Slovakia out of the tournament. His three goals at the tournament earned him the golden boot award, alongside five other players.

Ivan Nikolayevich Miroshnichenko (; born 4 February 2004) is a Russian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Hershey Bears of the American Hockey League (AHL) and is under contract as a prospect for the Washington Capitals of the National Hockey League (NHL). Outside of the NHL, Miroshnichenko played for Avangard Omsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Miroshnichenko is tied with John Brackenborough for having the longest non-hypinated surname in NHL history. Before playing in the NHL, Miroshnichenko played one season with Avangard Omsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). He was drafted 20th overall by the Washington Capitals in the 2022 NHL entry draft. On 1 May 2023, Miroshnichenko signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Capitals. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Hershey Bears. On 20 December 2023, the Capitals called him up and Miroshnichenko made his NHL debut in a 3–2 overtime win against the New York Islanders. On 7 March 2024, Miroshnichenko scored his first NHL goal against Alex Nedeljkovic in a 6–0 win against the Pittsburgh Penguins. He helped the Hershey Bears during the playoffs. They defeated the Lehigh Valley Phantoms, Hartford Wolf Pack, and Cleveland Monsters. They went on to defeat the Coachella Valley Firebirds four games to two in the Final to win the Calder Cup. In March 2022, Miroshnichenko was diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma. The diagnosis caused him to cut his season with Omskie Krylia of the All-Russian Hockey League (VHL) short. He recieved treatment in Germany which caused his cancer to go into full remission.

Ivan Vladimirovich Provorov (; born 13 January 1997) is a Russian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Columbus Blue Jackets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Philadelphia Flyers. Before playing in the NHL, Provorov played one season with the Cedar Rapids RoughRiders of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two seasons with the Brandon Wheat Kings of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time his teams. With the Wheat Kings, he won the Bill Hunter Memorial Trophy as the WHL's defenceman of the year. He was drafted 7th overall by the Philadelphia Flyers in the 2015 NHL entry draft. On 3 July 2015, Provorov signed a one-year entry-level contract to join the Flyers. On 14 October 2016, Provorov made his NHL debut in a 4–2 win against the Los Angeles Kings. During the second period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Mark Streit goal. On 23 November, Provorov scored his first NHL goal against Andrei Vasilevskiy in a 4–2 loss against the Tampa Bay Lightning. On 13 September 2019, Provorov signed a six-year, $40.5 million contract to stay with the Flyers. On 6 June 2023, Provorov was involved in a three-team trade with the Columbus Blue Jackets and Los Angeles Kings. The Flyers traded Provorov to the Blue Jackets. The Kings recieved Kevin Connauton and Hayden Hodgson, and the Flyers recieved Helge Grans, Cal Petersen, Sean Walker, a 2023 first-round draft pick, a 2024 second-round draft pick, and either a 2024 or 2025 conditional second-round draft pick. The Kings also retained 30% of Provorov's contract. On 1 July 2025, Provorov signed a seven-year, $59.5 million contract to stay with the Blue Jackets.

Ivan Vazquez Basurco (born February 11, 1975 in San Sebastian) is a 7-per-team football player from Spain. He has a disability: he has cerebral palsy and is a C7 type player. He played 7-per-team football at the 1996 Summer Paralympics. His team finished third after they played the United States and won 2-1. He played 7-per-team football at the 2000 Summer Paralympics. His team finished 6.

Ivan Zaytsev (born in Spoleto, Italy, 2 October 1988) is an Italian volleyball player. His parents originally come from Russia. He is a member of Italy's national volleyball team and the Italian club Sir Safety Umbria Volley. Zaytsev won a bronze medal at the Olympic Games in London in 2012. He won a silver medal at the European Championship (2011, 2013), and bronze medal at the World League (2013, 2014). He won the Italian Championship in 2014.

Ivan Stoyanov (; 20 January 1949 – 10 December 2017) was a Bulgarian footballer. He played as a midfielder. At club level, he played for Spartak Sofia and Levski Sofia. He also played for the Bulgaria national team in the 1974 FIFA World Cup. He was born in Sofia. Stoyanov died on 10 December 2017, at the age of 68.

Ivan Kolev Vutsov (; 14 December 1939 – 18 January 2019) was a Bulgarian football player and coach. He played for and later managed the Bulgarian national team. He played in three matches at the 1966 FIFA World Cup and for Levski Sofia.

Ivana Eloisa Müller (born 7 March 1974) is an Argentine volleyball player. She played at the 2002 FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship. She played for Phone Limited Modena and Figurella Firenze.

Ivan Stepanovich Utrobin (March 10, 1934 – June 25, 2020) was a Soviet cross-country skier. He competed during the early 1960s, training at VSS Trud in Moscow Oblast. He earned a bronze medal in the 4 x 10 km event at 1964 Winter Olympics in Innsbruck. Utrobin died on June 25, 2020 at the age of 86.

Ivana Plchotová (born 30 October 1982) is a Czech volleyball player. She played at the 2007 Women's European Volleyball Championship, 2009 Women's European Volleyball Championship, 2010 FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship, 2011 Women's European Volleyball Championship, 2013 Women's European Volleyball Championship, and 2015–16 CEV Women's Champions League. She played for MKS Dąbrowa Górnicza and CS Volei Alba Blaj.

Ivan Toplak (Serbian Cyrillic: Иван Toплaк; 21 September 1931 — 26 July 2021) was a Serbian football player and manager. Toplak played for NK Olimpija Ljubljana and Red Star Belgrade. He also represented the Yugoslavia national team. Toplak was born in Belgrade, Yugoslavia. Toplak died on 26 July 2021 in Maribor, Slovenia at the age of 89. Ivan Georgiev Zafirov (; 30 December 1947 – 15 October 2025) was a Bulgarian footballer. He played 50 times for Bulgaria, including at the 1974 FIFA World Cup and at the 1968 Summer Olympics, where he won a silver medal. Zafirov died on 15 October 2025, at the age of 77.

Ivan Thys (29 April 1897 – 15 February 1982) was a Belgian footballer. He played as a forward for Beerschot between 1919 and 1931, where he scored 132 goals in 203 games. He was also capped 20 times for Belgium between 1921 and 1926. He was the father of Belgian footballer and manager Guy Thys.
