Jason Culina (born 5 August 1980) is a former Australian soccer player and coach. Score and result list Australia's goal tally first, score column indicates score after Culina goal. Gold Coast United Player of the Year: 2009–10

Jarvis Green (born January 12, 1979) is a former American football player. He was a defensive end for the New England Patriots and Denver Broncos., He is 6'3 and weighs 285 pounds. He was born in Thibodaux, Louisana. He is 31 years old. He went to Louisana State University.

Jason Paul Collins (December 2, 1978 – May 12, 2026) was an American basketball player. He was a center for the Brooklyn Nets of the National Basketball Association (NBA). Collins was openly gay during the final years of his career which made him the first publicly gay athlete to play in any of the four major North American pro sports leagues and the first openly gay basketball player in the NBA. Collins played college basketball for Stanford University and was named to the All-Pac-10 first team in 2001. He was drafted by the New Jersey Nets with the 18th overall pick in the 2001 NBA Draft. He helped the Nets reach the NBA finals in 2001 but they were swept by the Los Angeles Lakers. He played 7 seasons with the Nets and he was traded with cash considerations to the Memphis Grizzlies for Stromile Swift. He played 31 games for the Grizzlies and then he was traded to the Minnesota Timberwolves in an eight-player deal involving Kevin Love and O. J. Mayo. When his contract expired at the end of the 2008–09 NBA season, the Timberwolves didn't re-sign him and he signed with the Atlanta Hawks on September 2, 2009. He played 3 seasons with the Hawks and signed an undisclosed deal with the Boston Celtics. He was traded by the Celtics to the Washington Wizards on February 21, 2013 for Jordan Crawford. After the 2012–13 NBA season concluded, Collins publicly came out as gay. He became a free agent and did not play again until February 2014, when he signed with the Nets. He became the first publicly gay athlete to play in any of the four major North American pro sports leagues. In 2014, Collins was featured on the cover of Time "100 Most Influential People in the World". His twin brother Jarron Collins also played in the NBA. On April 29, 2013, Collins wrote the cover story of Sports Illustrated in which he publicly come out as gay. He became the first active male professional athlete in any of the four major North American pro sports leagues to come out. He said that he chose the jersey number 98 in honor of Matthew Shepard, a victim of a gay hate crime in 1998. Collins said that the number was "a statement to myself, my family and my friends". In September 2025, Collins was diagnosed with glioblastoma, an aggressive form of brain cancer. He died from the disease on May 12, 2026 at his home in Los Angeles, California at the age of 47.

Jason Raymond Bay (born September 20, 1978) is a Canadian-American former professional baseball left fielder. Bay played in Major League Baseball (MLB) for the San Diego Padres, Pittsburgh Pirates, Boston Red Sox, New York Mets and Seattle Mariners. Bay was the National League Rookie of the Year in 2004 and he won the Silver Slugger Award in 2009. He is a three-time MLB All-Star and a three-time Tip O'Neill Award winner as the best Canadian baseball player. Bay debuted with the Padres on May 23, 2003, getting his first major league hit, a home run, in the ninth inning. Two days later, he suffered a broken right wrist after being hit by a pitch. On August 26, 2003, Bay was traded to the Pittsburgh Pirates, along with Óliver Pérez and Cory Stewart in exchange for Brian Giles. He finished the season with a.287 batting average, four home runs, and 14 RBI in 30 games. On July 31, 2008, Bay and a player to be named later (Josh Wilson)[8] were traded to the Boston Red Sox in a three team deal that sent Manny Ramirez to the Los Angeles Dodgers and Andy LaRoche with Bryan Morris to the Pittsburgh Pirates from the Dodgers and Brandon Moss with Craig Hansen to the Pirates from the Red Sox.

Jasmijn Lau (born 11 March 1999) is a Dutch long distance runner. Lau represents the Netherlands at international competitions. Lau beame multiple times national champion in the 10000 metres. She became under-23 European Champion at the 2021 European Athletics U23 Championships in the 10000 metres event. After a long injury she competed at the 2022 European Athletics Championships in the 10,000 metres event.

Jason Matthew Jaspers (born April 8, 1981 in Thunder Bay, Ontario), is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre who is currently playing for Kölner Haie (the Cologne Sharks) of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga. Jaspers was drafted 71st overall by the Phoenix Coyotes in the 1999 NHL Entry Draft. He was drafted from the Sudbury Wolves of the Ontario Hockey League. Jaspers made his professional start in the 2001–02 season with the Coyotes affiliate the Springfield Falcons of the American Hockey League. Jaspers made his National Hockey League (NHL) start in the same season, after he received his first NHL assignment on January 20, 2002. Jaspers then spent the next four years primarily with the Falcons of the American Hockey League. Unable to make the NHL regularly he was traded by the Coyotes to the Tampa Bay Lightning for Jarrod Skalde on July 25, 2005. Jason however, never played a game with the Lightning, playing for their affiliate coincidentally still the Springfield Falcons. Jaspers finally left the Falcons, ranking second in all-time appearances, in the 2006–07 season when he signed with German team Adler Mannheim, on July 6, 2006. After three years with Adler Mannheim signed on 6 April 2009 with Kölner Haie. In July 2008 Jason married his highschool sweetheart, Morgan McKee. Morgan is from Sudbury, Ontario where Jason played junior hockey for the Sudbury Wolves. Currently they have no children and live in Germany.

Jason Lowndes (14 December 1994 – 22 December 2017) was an Australian cyclist. He was born in Kalgoorlie, Western Australia. He rode professionally for Garneau–Québecor, Drapac Professional Cycling and Israel Cycling Academy teams. Lowndes died after being hit from behind by a car near Bendigo, Victoria at the age of 23.

Jason Marcano (30 December 1983 – 30 May 2019) was a Trinidadian footballer. He played as a forward. Marcano was born in Arima. He played for W Connection, San Juan Jabloteh, St. Ann's Rangers and Central between 2005 and 2018. He played for Trinidad and Tobago from 2007 to 2016, making 12 appearances. On 30 May 2019, Marcano was killed in a car crash near Arouca.

Jason Daniel Kendall (born June 26, 1974) is an American former professional baseball catcher. He played in Major League Baseball (MLB) from 1996 through 2010 for the Pittsburgh Pirates, Oakland Athletics, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers, and Kansas City Royals. He is the son of former catcher Fred Kendall, who played in the majors from 1969–1980. Not known for his batting abilities and lacking in power, Kendall was a great defensive catcher.

Jason Nicholas Doig (born January 29, 1977) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey player who played in the National Hockey League with the Winnipeg Jets, Phoenix Coyotes, New York Rangers and the Washington Capitals. 1993 Under-17 World Hockey Challenge, Team Quebec - Gold Medal 1994 Under-18 Copa Mexico, Team Canada - Gold Medal 1996 QMJHL President's Cup, Granby Predators 1996 Memorial Cup Championship, Granby Predators 1997 Under-20 World Junior Championship, Team Canada - Gold Medal 2007 Spengler Cup, Team Canada - Silver Medal

Sir Jason Francis Kenny, (born 23 March 1988) is an English track cyclist. Kenny is the record holder of most Olympic gold medals (7) and medals overall (9) for a British athlete. He is married to cyclist Laura Kenny.

Jason Fram (born April 23, 1995) is a Canadian-born Chinese professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Kunlun Red Star of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the major leagues, Fram played parts of 5 seasons with the Spokane Chiefs of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He would win the Canada West Defenseman of the Year Award in 2018. He was not drafted by an NHL team. He would be invited to the training camp for the San Jose Sharks. The Sharks would send Fram down to their AHL-affiliate San Jose Barracuda on December 8, 2016. He would play 2 games with them. On December 8, Fram would be released from his AHL contract. In 2016, Fram would play college hockey at the University of Alberta with the Golden Bears. During his time there, he would win the David Johnston University Cup after they defeated the St. Francis Xavier X-Men 4 games to 2. On May 30, 2019, Fram signed with Kunlun Red Star of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL).

Antonio Jason LaBarbera (born January 18, 1980) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey goaltender. He played parts of 13 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the New York Rangers, Los Angeles Kings, Vancouver Canucks, Phoenix Coyotes, Edmonton Oilers, and Anaheim Ducks. Before playing in the NHL, LaBarbera played parts of one season with the Tri-City Americans, four seasons with the Portland Winter Hawks, and one season with the Spokane Chiefs of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with his teams. He was named to the WHL All-Star Team in 2000. He was drafted 66th overall by the New York Rangers in the 1998 NHL entry draft. On October 14, 2000, LaBarbera made his NHL debut in relief of Kirk McLean, stopping all 2 shots he faced in a 8–6 loss against the Pittsburgh Penguins. After the game, the Rangers sent him down to play for their ECHL and AHL-affiliates Charlotte Checkers and Hartford Wolf Pack. He had successful time with the Wolf Pack, winning the Les Cunningham Award as AHL MVP and the Aldege "Baz" Bastien Memorial Award as the best goaltender in the AHL. On September 12, 2003, LaBarbera signed a contract to stay with the Rangers. On August 2, 2005, LaBarbera signed a two-year, $1.5 million contract to join the Los Angeles Kings. On April 17, 2006, he stopped all 31 shots in a in a 4–0 win against the San Jose Sharks to earn his first NHL shutout. During his time with the Kings, LaBarbera served as a backup goaltender for Mathieu Garon. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Manchester Monarchs. On December 30, 2008, the Kings traded LaBarbera to his hometown team Vancouver Canucks in exchange for a 2009 seventh-round draft pick. He played 9 regular seasons games with the Canucks, posting a 3–2–2 record with a 2.66 goals against average and a.915 save percentage. On July 1, 2009, LaBarbera signed a two-year, $2 million contract to join the Phoenix Coyotes. The Coyotes signed him to be a backup goaltender for Ilya Bryzgalov. On June 6, 2011, LaBarbera signed a two-year, $2.5 million contract to stay with the Coyotes. On July 5, 2013, LaBarbera signed a one-year, $1 million contract to join the Edmonton Oilers. He played 7 regular seasons games with the Oilers before being sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Oklahoma City Barons. On December 14, the Oilers traded LaBarbera to the Chicago Blackhawks in exchange for future considerations. LaBarbera never played a game for the Blackhawks and was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Rockford IceHogs. On July 1, 2014, LaBarbera signed a one-year, $750,000 contract to join the Anaheim Ducks. He played 5 regular season games and spent most of his time playing for their AHL-affiliate Norfolk Admirals. On July 1, 2015, LaBarbera signed a one-year contract to join the Philadelphia Flyers. He never played a game with the Flyers and was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Lehigh Valley Phantoms. On September 25, 2021, LaBarbera announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey and was accepting a job to become the goaltending coach of the Calgary Hitmen of the Western Hockey League. On December 16, 2020, LaBarbera signed a contract to become the goaltending coach for the Calgary Flames.

Jason Dickinson (born July 4, 1995) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Dallas Stars, Vancouver Canucks, and Chicago Blackhawks. Before playing in the NHL, Dickinson played four seasons with the Guelph Storm of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with the Storm. He was named to the Second All-Rookie Team. He was drafted 29th overall by Dallas Stars in the 2013 NHL entry draft. On May 29, 2014, Dickinson signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Stars. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Texas Stars. On April 7, 2016, Dallas called him up and Dickinson made his NHL debut in a 4–2 win against the Colorado Avalanche. During the first period, he scored his first NHL goal against Carey Price. On July 6, 2018, Dickinson signed a one-year, $875,000 contract to stay with the Stars. On July 11, 2019, Dickinson signed a two-year contract to stay with the Stars. On July 17, 2021, the Stars traded Dickinson to the Vancouver Canucks in the 2021 third-round draft pick. He scored 5 goals and recorded 6 assists in 52 regular season games for the Canucks. On October 7, 2022, the Canucks traded Dickinson along with a 2024 second-round draft pick to the Chicago Blackhawks in exchange for Riley Stillman. On January 16, 2024, Dickinson signed a two-year, $8.5 million contract to stay with the Blackhawks. On March 4, 2026, the Blackhawks traded Dickinson along with Colton Dach to the Edmonton Oilers in exchange for Andrew Mangiapane and a 2027 conditional first-round draft pick. On June 21, 2026, Dickinson signed a two-year, $20 million contract to stay with the Oilers.

Jason Varitek (born April 11, 1972 in Rochester, Michigan) is an American retired baseball player who played in the MLB. Varitek played for the Boston Red Sox up until his retirement in March 2012. Varitek was called up from Triple A Pawtucket on September 24, 1997, for one game. In 1998, he and catcher Scott Hatteberg were the starting catchers. That season, Varitek played 86 games, while Hatteberg played 76. Varitek had a good spring training in 1999. Because of that, he became the starting catcher. Varitek had a great season in 1999. Varitek played in 144 games. He hit a.269 batting average, with 20 home runs and 76 RBIs. Varitek went 5–21 with 3 RBI in the 1999 ALDS playing. the Cleveland Indians. He then went 4–20 with 1 RBI in the ALCS playing the New York Yankees.
Jason Roberts (born 25 January 1978) is a retired Grenadian football player. Scores and results list Grenada's goal tally first, score column indicates score after each Roberts goal.

Jason Paul Taylor (born September 1, 1974) is a former American football defensive end and linebacker who played in NFL for the Miami Dolphins, Washington Redskins and New York Jets. Taylor was drafted by the Miami Dolphins in the third round (73rd pick overall) of the 1997 NFL Draft. He also performed on the sixth season of Dancing with the Stars and finished as the runner up to Kristi Yamaguchi. On December 28, 2011, Taylor announced that he would retire at the end of the 2011 season.

Jason Rocco Anthony Spezza (born June 13, 1983 in Mississauga, Ontario) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey centre. He played a total of 19 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Ottawa Senators, Dallas Stars and Toronto Maple Leafs. He began his hockey career with the Brampton Battalion of the Ontario Hockey League (NHL). He also played for the Mississauga Ice Dogs for 2 seasons, the Windsor Spitfires for 2 seasons and the Belleville Bulls for 1 season. He entered the draft in 2001 and he was drafted with the 2nd overall by the Ottawa Senators in the 2001 NHL Entry Draft. He was assigned to the Grand Rapids Griffins, the farm team of the Senators. He was called up to the Senators and made his NHL debut in the 2002-03 NHL season. He played 33 games with the Senators and played most of the season with Ottawa's new affiliate, Binghamton Senators. He was called up and played two seasons with the Senators and was sent down to the Binghamton Senators to play a season. After that he joined the Ottawa's main roster full-time. Spezza was on the cover of 2007 video game, NHL 2K8. He married his girlfriend Jennifer on July 25, 2009. They have two daughters Sophia Donna Spezza (born June 8, 2010) and Nicola Patricia Spezza (born April 1, 2012). On July 1, 2014, after Spezza had requested a trade, the Senators traded him along with Ludwig Karlsson to the Dallas Stars in exchange for Alex Chiasson, Alex Guptill, Nicolas Paul and a 2015 second-round pick to Ottawa. On May 29, 2022, Spezza announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey. After he retired, he became an assistant to Leafs general manager Kyle Dubas. On May 19, 2023, Spezza stepped down when Dubas was fired.

Jason Matthew Vargas (born February 2, 1983) is an American professional baseball player. He plays for the Kansas City Royals. He joined the Florida Marlins in the 2004 MLB Draft. Vargas made his MLB debut in 2005. He recorded two career starts with the New York Mets in 2007 and was sent to the Seattle Mariners in 2009.

Jason Anthoney Richardson (born January 20, 1981) is an American former professional basketball player. He played 14 seasons in the National Basketball Association (NBA). Richardson was taken by the Golden State Warriors as the fifth overall pick in the 2001 NBA draft after playing college basketball for Michigan State University. He won the NBA Dunk Contest in both 2002 and 2003, becoming the second player, after Michael Jordan, to win the competition back-to-back. Richardson has also played for the Charlotte Bobcats, Phoenix Suns, Orlando Magic, and the Philadelphia 76ers.
Jason Jonathan Roy (born 21 July 1990) is a cricketer from Durban, South Africa. He plays for England in One Day International (ODI) and Twenty20 International (T20I) cricket.

Jason James Tindall (born 15 November 1977) is an English professional football manager and former player, who is currently the assistant manager at Newcastle United and the acting manager at Newcastle United until Howe has fully recovery.

Jason Williams (born August 11, 1980) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey right winger. He played parts of 11 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Detroit Red Wings, Chicago Blackhawks, Atlanta Thrashers, Columbus Blue Jackets, Dallas Stars, and Pittsburgh Penguins. Outside of the NHL, Williams played for Porin Ässät of the SM-liiga, HC Ambrì-Piotta of the National League A (NLA), Kölner Haie of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL), Ritten Sport of the Alps Hockey League (AlpsHL), the Nottingham Panthers of the Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL), and the Brantford Blast and Dundas Real McCoys of the Allan Cup Hockey (ACH). Williams is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with Red Wings in 2002. Before playing in the NHL, Williams played parts of four seasons with the Peterborough Petes of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with the Petes. He was named to the OHL Third All-Star Team and was also awarded the OHL Plus/Minus Award in the 1999–2000 season. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On September 18, 2000, Williams signed a contract to join the Detroit Red Wings of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Cincinnati Mighty Ducks. On November 20, 2000, the Red Wings called him up and Williams made his NHL debut in a 6–3 win over with the Nashville Predators. During the game, Williams recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Martin Lapointe goal. On March 6, 2002, Williams scored his first NHL goal against Sébastien Centomo in a 6–2 win over with the Toronto Maple Leafs. He helped the Red Wings when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Vancouver Canucks, St. Louis Blues, and Colorado Avalanche. They went on to defeat the Carolina Hurricanes four games to one in the Final to win the Stanley Cup. On September 15, 2003, Williams signed a contract to stay with the Red Wings. After the NHL went entered a lockout, Williams decided to head overseas and signed a contract to play for Porin Ässät of the SM-liiga. With Ässät, he scored 26 goals and recorded 17 assists for 42 points in 43 games. He returned to the Red Wings after the lockout ended. On July 29, 2004, Williams signed a contract to stay with the Red Wings. On October 22, 2005, Williams recorded his first career hat-trick in a 6–0 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets. On August 16, 2005, Williams signed a two-year, $3.2 million contract to stay with the Red Wings. On November 8, 2006, Williams was checked from behind by Raffi Torres, causing his head to hit the ice hard. Williams was left with a first-degree concussion, lacerations to his face, and had to be stretchered off of the ice. On February 26, 2007, the Red Wings entered in a three-team trade and traded Williams to the Chicago Blackhawks in exchange for Kyle Calder. He played parts of two seasons with the Blackhawks, scoring 17 goals and recording 25 assists for 42 points. On July 13, 2008, Williams signed a one-year, $2.2 million contract to join the Atlanta Thrashers. He scored 7 goals and recorded 11 assists for 18 points in his 41 regular season game played with the Thrashers. On January 14, 2009, the Thrashers traded Williams to the Columbus Blue Jackets in exchange for Clay Wilson and a 2009 sixth-round draft pick. He scored 12 goals and recorded 17 assists for 29 points in his 39 regular season game played with the Blue Jackets. On August 6, 2009, Williams signed a one-year contract to rejoin the Red Wings. On November 7, Williams suffered a fractured right fibula after his leg ended up buckling and getting caught under his body as he crashed into the boards. On February 12, 2011, Williams signed a one-year, $500,000 contract to join the Dallas Stars. He scored 2 goals and recorded 3 assists for 5 points in his 27 regular season game played with the Stars. On July 26, 2011, Williams signed a one-year, $600,000 two-way contract to join the Pittsburgh Penguins. He played 8 games with Pittsburgh and spent most of his time playing for their AHL-affiliate Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins. He decided to head overseas and signed a contract to play for HC Ambrì-Piotta of the National League A (NLA). On July 16, 2015, Williams signed a one-year contract to join Kölner Haie of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL). Williams retired from playing professional ice hockey in 2017.

Jason Polin (born June 17, 1999) is an American professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Buffalo Sabres of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Colorado Avalanche. Before playing in the NHL, Polin played three season with the Cedar Rapids RoughRiders of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and four years with the Omaha Mavericks of the National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Mavericks, he was named the NCHC Player of the Year and NCHC Forward of the Year. He was also named to the All-NCHC First Team and an AHCA West Second Team All-American. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On March 2, 2025, Polin signed an one-year entry-level contract to join the Colorado Avalanche of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Colorado Eagles. On January 8, 2024, the Avalanche called him up and Polin made his NHL debut in a 4–3 shootout win against the Boston Bruins. On January 16, Polin scored his first NHL goal against Mads Søgaard in a 7–4 win against the Ottawa Senators. On February 4, 2026, Polin signed a one-year contract to join the Buffalo Sabres.

Jason Robertson (born July 22, 1999) is an American professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Dallas Stars of the National Hockey League (NHL). Robertson is a one-time All-Star, being named one in 2023. Before playing in the NHL, Robertson played four seasons with the Kingston Frontenacs and one season with the Niagara IceDogs of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with his teams. He won the CHL Top Scorer Award and Eddie Powers Memorial Trophy as the OHL's top scorer. He was also named to the OHL First All-Star Team and OHL Third All-Star Team. He was drafted 39th overall by the Dallas Stars of the 2017 NHL entry draft. On March 3, 2018, Robertson signed an three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Stars. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Texas Stars. On February 13, 2020, Dallas called him up and Robertson made his NHL debut in a 3–2 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs. During the third period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Tyler Seguin goal. On February 7, 2021, Robertson scored his first NHL goal against Malcolm Subban in a 2–1 overtime loss against the Chicago Blackhawks. On March 4, 2022, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 4–3 overtime win against the Winnipeg Jets. On October 5, Robertson signed a four-year, $7.75 million contract to stay with the Stars. On January 5, 2023, Robertson was selected to play in his first All-Star game. On July 22, 2026, Robertson signed a one-year, $12 million contract to stay with the Stars.

Jassen A. Cullimore (born December 4, 1972 in Simcoe, Ontario) is a Canadian retired professional ice hockey defenceman that last played for the Iserlohn Roosters of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga. He formerly played Vancouver Canucks from 1994-1996, the Montreal Canadiens from 1996-1997, the Tampa Bay Lightning from 1997-2003 winning the Stanley Cup with them during the 2003-04 NHL season, the Chicago Blackhawks from 2005-06, the Florida Panthers from 2007-08 and signed a two-way contract returning to the Chicago Blackhawks which he played one season with in 2010.

Jasur Alijanov (uz: Jasur Alijonov: ru: Алижонов Жасур Батыровыч, born May 12, 1988) is an Uzbekistani Mixed martial arts coach and trainer. He is a former boxer. and featherweight kickboxer. Alijanov trains UFC fighter Makhmud Muradov and other ONE Championship fighters. Jasur Alijanov was born on May 12, 1988 in Tashkent, Uzbekistan. He started practicing Kickboxing, Unifight and Boxing when he was 12. In 2008 he made his debut in professional boxing. After unsuccessful debut in first professional bout, he made his win on his second bout on May 5, 2008 over Abdumanap Kuchkarov. After 8 fights, 6 wins he had to end his professional boxing career due to injury. After ending his professional sports career, he began a professional coaching career in Kickboxing, Boxing and MMA (Mixed Martial Arts). Immediately after his active career, he began a new career at the Legion Fight Club, where he trains UFC fighter Makhmud Muradov and Ramazonbek Temirov.

Jasprit Bumrah (born 6 December 1993) is an Indian cricketer who represents the Indian national team as a right-arm fast-medium bowler. He is recognized for his exceptional bowling skills, accurate yorkers, and unique bowling action. Bumrah has been considered one of the best bowlers in the world and has played a significant role in the success of the Indian cricket team across all formats. He plays for Mumbai Indians in the Indian premier league.

Jasper van der Werff (* 9 December 1998 in St. Gallen, Switzerland ) is a Swiss-Dutch football player. He plays for Universitatea Cluj in Romania. Van der Werff began his career at FC St. Gallen. After playing in the club's youth academy, he was promoted to the U-21 squad for the 2016/17 season. He made his debut for the U-21s in October 2016. After more than 20 appearances in the Swiss First League, van der Werff was included in the first-team squad for the first time in February 2018 against BSC Young Boys. That same month, he made his Super League debut, starting in the 22nd matchday of the 2017/18 season against FC Basel. For the 2018/19 season, he went to Austrian Bundesliga club FC Red Bull Salzburg. Initially he played for the feeder team FC Liefering in the second division. He made his debut for them in August 2018 against SK Vorwärts Steyr. He made his Bundesliga debut for the first team against TSV Hartberg on 18 August 2018. In the match against SK Sturm he suffered a serious injury and was sidelined for several months. In January 2020, he returned to Switzerland and was loaned to FC Basel for a year and a half. For the 2021/22 season, he was loaned out to German second-division side SC Paderborn 07. In May 2022, the German club signed him permanently. Within the league, he was loaned to Hansa Rostock for one season in the summer of 2023. He suffered relegation to the third division. After the loan ended, the player left SC Paderborn 07 went to Romanian first division club Universitatea Cluj.

Javed Akhtar (21 November 1940 – 8 July 2016) was a Pakistani cricketer. He played in one Test in 1962. He was an off spinner. He had success at first-class level, taking his wickets at an average of 18.17, but struggled in his only Test, failing to take a wicket. He played for the Pakistan national cricket team. He later became an umpire, standing in 18 Tests and 40 ODIs from 1980 to 1999.

Javier Otxoa Palacios (born August 30, 1974 in Vizcaya – August 24, 2018, Alhaurín de la Torre) was a cyclist from Spain. He was a race car driver before being run over by a car. After being run over by a car, he decided to be a cyclist all the time. He has a disability: He has cerebral palsy and is a C3 type cyclist. He competed at the 2004 Summer Paralympics in cycling. He was the number 1 racer to finish in the Combined Road race. He was the number 2 cyclist in the Individual Pursuit track race. He competed at the 2008 Summer Paralympics in cycling. He was the number 1 racer to finish in the Road Trial race. He was the number 2 cyclist in the road race. Otxoa won two gold medals and two silver medals at the 2004 Summer Paralympics and the 2008 Summer Paralympics. Otxoa died on 24 August 2018 in Alhaurín de la Torre, Spain from sepsis at the age of 43.

Javier Porras Santana (born August 22, 1981 in Olot, Girona) is a athlete from Spain. He has a disability: he cannot see and is a T11/B1 type athlete. He competed in the 2004 Summer Paralympics in Athens, Greece. He competed at the 2008 Summer Paralympics in Beijing, China and was the third best athlete in the triple jump. He competed at the 2012 Summer Paralympics.

Javier Goñi Lopéz (born 12 April 1986 in Madrid) is a swimmer from Spain. He has a disability: He cannot see everything and is an S11/B1 type swimmer. He raced at the 2004 Summer Paralympics in Athens, Greece. He finished second in the 100 meter backstroke race.

Javier Astúa Araya (6 November 1968 – 4 January 2022) was a Costa Rican professional footballer. He played as a forward. He played for the Costa Rica national football team between 1992 until 1994, making thirteen appearances. Astúa died on 4 January 2022 from heart disease in San José, Costa Rica, at the age of 53.

Javier Fernández Cabrera Martín Peñato (born 4 October 1984) is a Spanish professional football coach. He currently manages the Bangladesh national football team. Cabrera is an UEFA Pro License Coach with wide experience in both professional and grassroots football projects. Cabrera also has a reputation as a football analyst. Cabrera has the experience of working as an expert analyst for Opta Sports and he also has a bachelor's degree in football as well as advertising and marketing. Cabrera worked as a technical director and as an assistant coach for Indian side Sporting Clube de Goa, from 2013 to 2015. In 2016, he was appointed as the manager for Spanish club CF Rayo Majadahonda and spent a year coaching the team, before leaving the club in 2017. Moreover, he was the head coach of FC Barcelona Academy in Northern Virginia for 4 months in 2018. From 2018, Cabrera acted as the Elite Academy coach of La Liga side Deportivo Alavés, before being announced as the Bangladesh national football team head coach in 8 January 2022. On 19 January 2022, Cabrera finished his contract signing and was officially made the Bangladesh national football team head coach. Upon signing the contract, Cabrera's first task was to observe the training sessions of all the Bangladesh Premier League teams, in order to scout for new talents.

Javier Berasaluce Marquiegui (4 January 1931 – 8 February 2022) was a Spanish footballer. He played as a goalkeeper. He played in La Liga with Deportivo Alavés, Real Madrid and Racing de Santander. His career began in 1951 and he retired in 1963. Berasaluce died on 8 February 2022, at the age of 91.

Francisco Javier Imbroda Ortiz (8 January 1961 – 2 April 2022) was a Spanish basketball coach and politician. He was the sixth coach with the most games directed in the Liga ACB. He was born in Melilla, Spain. He was a member of the Andalusian Parliament since 2018 and Regional Minister of Culture and Sports since 2019. Imbroda died on 2 April 2022 in Malaga, Spain from prostate cancer, aged 61.

José Javier Sánchez Galindo (26 November 1947 – 29 September 2025) was a Mexican footballer. He played for Mexico at the 1968 Summer Olympics. He died in September 2025, at the age of 77. Primera División de México: 1968–69, 1970, 1971–72, 1972–73, 1973–74 CONCACAF Champions' Cup: 1969, 1970, 1971

Jawad El Yamiq (; born 29 February 1992) is a Moroccan professional footballer who plays as a centre-back for Saudi club Al-Wehda and the Morocco national team. He was part of the Moroccan national team that played in the 2018 African Nations Championship and 2022 FIFA World Cup. On 10 November 2022, he was named in Morocco's 26-man squad for the 2022 FIFA World Cup that was scheduled to be held in Qatar. After Morocco defeated Canada 2–1 in a World Cup match, El Yamiq made headlines as he was seen waving a Palestinian Flag during the post-match celebrations.

Augustine Azuka Okocha (; born 14 August 1973), commonly known as Jay-Jay Okocha, is a Nigerian former professional footballer. He played as an attacking midfielder. He played 73 times for the Nigeria national team between 1993 and 2006, scoring 14 times. He was a member of three FIFA World Cup squads. He is considered as one of the greatest football players from Africa. Okocha is gifted with remarkable technique and speed. He is regarded as one of the best dribblers in history. He was also an expert in long-range shots, step-over skills and set pieces. In 1990 Okocha moved as a youth player from the Nigerian club Enugu Rangers to then third division club Borussia Neunkirchen. There he made his debut as a 17-year-old in the Oberliga team.In his first season in Neunkirchen he caused a sensation with his dribbles and goals, sometimes from more than 30 meters goal distance in the Oberliga Südwest. The coach of league rivals Eintracht Trier, Dragoslav Stepanović steered him to Frankfurt in 1992. He first played as a contract amateur for Eintracht Frankfurt. On September 26, 1992 he played against Werder Bremen for the first time in the Bundesliga. He became known for sensational dribbles and made the headlines. His goal to make it 3-1 against Karlsruhe SC in the Bundesliga game on August 31, 1993 was spectacular. He played around the opposing defenders in the penalty area and made goalkeeper Oliver Kahn run back and forth several times with body tricks and sudden changes of direction before he finally got the ball shot in goal. The viewers of the sports show voted this goal of the year 1993. At the beginning of December 1994, he made headlines when he showed his solidarity with his teammates Anthony Yeboah and Maurizio Gaudino He refused special training ordered by coach Jupp Heynckes and participation in the subsequent Bundesliga game. This resulted in the dismissal of Yeboah and Gaudino. After Eintracht was relegated to the 2nd Bundesliga, Okocha played for the Turkish first division club Fenerbahçe Istanbul from 1996 to 1998. He accepted Turkish citizenship. He moved to Paris Saint-Germain in 1998 for 22 million marks. Jay-Jay Okocha made 90 appearances (18 goals) in the 1st Bundesliga for Eintracht Frankfurt from 1992 to 1996. In the Premier League he completed 124 games ( 14 goals) for Bolton Wanderers from 2002. He was voted BBC African Footballer of the Year in 2003 and 2004. At the end of the 2005/06 season, however, his contract was not extended by the "Trotters", although he was still one of the regulars. After a year in Qatar, he signed a one-year contract with English second division side Hull City for the 2007/08 season. With the new club, he was promoted to the Premier League. Okocha made his official debut for Nigeria in their 2–1 1994 FIFA World Cup Qualifier away loss against Ivory Coast in May 1993. It was not until his second cap and home debut that he became a favourite with the Nigerian supporters. With Nigeria trailing 1–0 against Algeria, in a match they needed to win, he scored from a direct free kick to equalise. He helped the team to a 4–1 win, securing qualification to their first World Cup. In 1994, he was a member of both the victorious 1994 African Cup of Nations squad and the World Cup squad who made it to the second round before they lost in a dramatic match against eventual runners-up Italy. In 1996, Okocha became a key member of an arguably more successful Nigerian side, their Olympic gold winning side at the Atlanta Games. This was nicknamed the Dream Team by the Nigerian press after the USA 1992 Olympic gold winning basketball team. In the 1998 FIFA World Cup hosted by France, Okocha played for a disappointing Super Eagles side. They failed to live up to expectations with less impressive performances save for their 3–2 opening win against Spain. This did not destroy interest in Okocha, who had entertained fans with his trademark skills and dribbles and went on to be named in the squad of the tournament. Okocha again joined the Super Eagles in the 2000 African Cup of Nations co-hosted with Ghana. He scored three goals in the tournament, two in the opening game against Tunisia. He was given a standing ovation by the nearly 60,000 attendance when he left the field. He made a return to the Super Eagles in his testimonial against an African select side in Warri. The game featured former players Daniel Amokachi, Alloysius Agu, John Fashanu, Benjani and Sulley Muntari. Nigeria won the game 2–1 with Okocha scoring the winning goal after appearing for the side in the second half. In March 2004, he was named one of the top 125 living footballers by Pelé. Jay Allen Bruce (born April 3, 1987) is an American professional baseball corner outfielder for the Philadelphia Phillies of Major League Baseball (MLB). Before he played for the Phillies, he played for the Cincinnati Reds, New York Mets, Cleveland Indians, and Seattle Mariners. The Reds chose Bruce in the first round, 12th overall pick, of the 2005 Major League Baseball draft (where teams chose their players). He started playing in MLB in 2008. Bruce has been named an All-Star three times during his career, and has won the Silver Slugger Award twice.

John William Johnstone Jr. (November 20, 1945 – September 26, 2020) was an American professional baseball player and television sports announcer. He was born in Manchester, Connecticut. He played in Major League Baseball as an outfielder from 1966 to 1985 for the California Angels, Chicago White Sox, Oakland Athletics, Philadelphia Phillies, New York Yankees, San Diego Padres, Los Angeles Dodgers, and Chicago Cubs. Johnstone died on September 26, 2020 from dementia and COVID-19 in Los Angeles, aged 74.

Jay Daniel Bouwmeester (born September 27, 1983) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey defenceman. He played parts of 17 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Florida Panthers, Calgary Flames, and St. Louis Blues. He is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with Blues in 2001. He is also a two-time All-Star, being named one in 2007 and 2009. Internationally, Bouwmeester played for Canada. He won a gold medal with them at the 2014 Winter Olympics and also winning back-to-back gold medals with them at the 2003 and 2004 World Championships. This made him a member of the Triple Gold Club. Before playing in the NHL, Bouwmeester played parts of four seasons with the Medicine Hat Tigers of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with the Tigers, being named to the WHL Eastern Conference First All-Star Team and also being selected to play in the NHL/NHL Top Prospects Game. He was drafted 3rd overall by the Florida Panthers in the 2002 NHL entry draft. On October 10, 2002, Bouwmeester made his NHL debut in a 4–3 overtime against the Tampa Bay Lightning. During the game, he also recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Niklas Hagman goal. On 6 December 2005, he scored his first NHL goal against Jocelyn Thibault in a 2–2 overtime tie against the Chicago Blackhawks. He did well in his rookie season and was named to the NHL All-Rookie Team. After the NHL entered a lockout, Bouwmeester decided to play for the Panthers' AHL-affiliate San Antonio Rampage. After the Rampage missed the playoffs, he was loaned tot he Chicago Wolves. He helped the Wolves during the playoffs. They defeated the Houston Aeros, Cincinnati Mighty Ducks, and Manitoba Moose. They were eventually swept and defeated four games to zero by the Philadelphia Phantoms in the Calder Cup Finals. Bouwmeester was very productive the next season, ending the season by scoring 5 goals and recording 41 assists for 46 points in 82 games which were all new career-highs for him. He was also selected to play in his first All-Star game that year. On July 28, 2008, Bouwmeester signed a one-year, $4.875 million to stay with the Panthers. He became the NHL's leading ironman after former leader Andrew Brunette was injured and also was selected for his second All-Star game. On June 27, 2009, the Panthers traded Bouwmeester to the Calgary Flames in exchange for Jordan Leopold and a 2009 third-round draft pick. On June 30, Bouwmeester signed a five-year, $33 million to stay with the Flames. On March 15, 2011, Bouwmeester broke Kārlis Skrastiņš's record and became the new NHL leader in games played for a defenceman after playing in his 486th straight regular season game. On April 1, 2013, the Flames traded Bouwmeester to the St. Louis Blues in exchange for Mark Cundari, Reto Berra and a 2013 first-round draft pick. On August 1, 2013, Bouwmeester signed a five-year, $27 million contract to stay with the Blues. On November 23, 2014, Bouwmeester's ironman streak was snapped at 737 straight regular season games after he suffered an injury during a game against the Ottawa Senators and was forced to miss the game. It was the fifth-longest streak in NHL history. On April 8, 2019, Bouwmeester signed a one-year, $3.25 million contract to stay with the Blues. He helped the Blues during the playoffs. They defeated the Winnipeg Jets, Dallas Stars, and the San Jose Sharks. They eventually went on to defeat the Boston Bruins four games to three in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Blues franchise history. During a game on February 11, 2020 against the Anaheim Ducks, Bouwmeester was on the bench when he went into cardiac arrest had to be revived with a defibulator. The game was later postponed and played again on March 11. On January 11, 2021, Bouwmeester announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey. On September 4, 2007, Bouwmeester pled guilty to one-count of Driving under the influence.

Jayde Appel is an Australian water polo player. She played for the Australian women's national water polo team in the 2013 World Aquatics Championships. She played for University of Southern California.

Jay Silverheels (born Harold Jay Smith, May 26, 1912 – March 5, 1980) was an Aboriginal Canadian actor and athlete. He was well known for his role as Tonto, the Native American sidekick of the Lone Ranger in the American western television series The Lone Ranger.

J. W. "Jay" Porter (January 17, 1933 – October 11, 2020) was an American Major League Baseball player. He appeared with the St. Louis Browns in 1952, Detroit Tigers between 1955 and 1957, Cleveland Indians in 1958, Washington Senators in 1959, and St. Louis Cardinals in 1959. Porter was born in Shawnee, Oklahoma. Porter died of respiratory failure on October 11, 2020 in Jupiter, Florida at the age of 87.

Jamie White (born 9 October 1992) is a New Zealand professional wrestler. He currently wrestles for All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and competes under the ring name Jay White. White has also competed in New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW), Ring of Honor (ROH), Revolution Pro Wrestling (RevPro), and Impact Wrestling. He has also competed on the independent circuit for many other promotions. White has won many championships in many different companies. In AEW, he is a one-time AEW World Trios Champion. In ROH, he was a one-time ROH World Six-Man Tag Team Champion. In New Japan, he is a one-time IWGP World Heavyweight Champion, one-time IWGP Heavyweight Champion, one-time IWGP Intercontinental Champion, one-time NEVER Openweight Champion, one-time IWGP United States Heavyweight Champion, and was a Fifth and First NJPW Triple Crown Champion. On the 9 February 2022 episode of Dynamite, White made his AEW debut. He ran in and helped Adam Cole and The Young Bucks in a beatdown of Trent Beretta and Rocky Romero. On the February 18 episode of Rampage, White made his AEW in-ring debut and defeated Beretta. He then traveled back to Japan to continue to working for New Japan Pro-Wrestling. He made his return to AEW on the April 20 episode of Dynamite where he along with Adam Cole, interrupted AEW owner and founder Tony Khan and Takami Ohbari's announcement of AEW×NJPW: Forbidden Door. At Forbidden Door, White successfully defended his IWGP World Heavyweight Championship against "Hangman" Adam Page, Kazuchika Okada, and Adam Cole in a four-way match. White officially left New Japan in 2023 and returned to AEW on the April 5, 2023 edition of Dynamite where he reunited with his fellow Bullet Club Gold member Juice Robinson. Tony Khan announced that Jay White had signed a contract to become a member of the roster. He began a feud with Ricky Starks and The Gunns (Austin and Colten Gunn) joined Bullet Club Gold. At Full Gear, White challeneged Maxwell Jacob Friedman for the AEW World Championship but lost the match. On January 17, 2024, White teamed with The Gunns and they defeated Mogul Embassy (Brian Cage, Kaun and Toa Liona) to become the new ROH World Six-Man Tag Team Champion. The team briefly joined forces with The Acclaimed to become the Bang Bang Scissor Gang before turning on them at Big Business after White defeated Darby Allin. AEW Executive Vice President Christopher Daniels stripped the three of the championships after White suffered an injury to his foot. White returned to AEW on the October 2 episode of Dynamite to save Juice Robinson from being beatdown by "Hangman" Adam Page. At Worlds End, White challenged Jon Moxley for the AEW World Championship but lost. At Grand Slam Australia, White teamed with Cope and lost to Death Riders (Jon Moxley and Claudio Castagnoli) in a Brisbane Brawl.

Jayden Oswin Adams (5 May 2001 – 11 July 2026) was a South African professional soccer player who played as a defensive midfielder. In 2020, Adams made his senior debut for the then recently promoted Stellenbosch F.C.. In 2023, he helped Stellenbosch win the Carling Knockout Cup. In January 2025, Adams joined the Mamelodi Sundowns based in Pretoria. In the same season he won the South African Premiership with the club. In May 2026, he won the CAF Champions League with the Sundowns after helping them defeat Moroccan-side AS FAR. In 2022, Adams made his senior debut for South Africa in a match against Mozambique. On 28 December 2023, Adams was named by Hugo Broos as part of his final 23-man squad for the Africa Cup of Nations. Adams was called up by South Africa to play in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, where he would play in all 3 of South Africa's group stage matches, helping them qualify for the knockout stages for the first time in their history, however, he would not play in the match against Canada. During his international career he earned a total 13 caps and scored 2 goals, with both being scored during 2026 World Cup qualifying matches. On 11 July 2026, Adams was found dead in home located in Schotsche Kloof, a suburb in central Cape Town, at the age of 25, leaving behind his partner, Aqueelah Adendorf, and a five-year old daughter. This came only 16 days after he had played in the group stage of the World Cup against South Korea. Prior to the quarterfinal match between Norway and England, a moment of silence was held for Adams. Another tribute was held for Adams in the quarterfinal match between Argentina and Switzerland. As of 12 July 2026, an official cause of death has yet to be released.

Jaycob Dalton Megna (born December 10, 1992) is an American professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Megna played one season with the Muskegon Lumberjacks of the United States Hockey League (USHL), as well as, three years with the Omaha Mavericks of the Western Collegiate Hockey Association (WCHA) and National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He was drafted 210th overall by the Anaheim Ducks of the 2012 NHL entry draft. On April 4, 2014, Megna signed an three-year, $2.36 million entry-level contract to join the Ducks. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Norfolk Admirals and San Diego Gulls. On February 4, 2026, the Ducks called him up and Megna made his NHL debut in a 4–0 win against the Chicago Blackhawks. On October 20, 2017, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Dennis Rasmussen goal in a 6–2 win against the Montreal Canadiens. On March 6, 2019, Megna scored his first NHL goal against Jordan Binnington in a 5–4 loss against the St. Louis Blues. On July 29, 2021, Megna signed a one-year contract to join the San Jose Sharks. On May 9, 2022, Megna signed a two-year contract to stay with the San Jose Sharks. On February 5, 2023, the Sharks traded Megna to the Seattle Kraken in exchange for a 2023 fourth-round draft pick. He played six regular season games with the Kraken. On January 2, 2024, the Kraken placed Megna onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Chicago Blackhawks. He recorded 2 assists in 44 regular season games for the Blackhawks. On July 5, 2024, Megna signed a two-year contract to join the Florida Panthers. He played 8 regular season games for the Panthers. On July 1, 2025, Megna signed a two-year contract to join the Vegas Golden Knights. He played 8 regular season games for the Panthers. Megna's older brother Jayson is also a professional hockey player.

Jayson Megna (born February 1, 1990) is an American professional ice hockey center. He currently plays for the Colorado Avalanche of the National Hockey League. He also played for Pittsburgh Penguins, Vancouver Canucks, and New York Rangers of the (NHL). He was born in Fort Lauderdale, Florida and grew up in Northbrook, Illinois. Before playing in the NHL, Megna played 2 seasons with the Cedar Rapids RoughRiders of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and half a year of college hockey with the University of Nebraska Omaha Mavericks. During his time with the Mavericks, Megna was named to the WCHA All-Rookie Team. He was not drafted but he signed a two-way contract with the Pittsburgh Penguins on August 1, 2012. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate, the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins. The Penguins called Megna up on October 24, 2013. Megna made his NH L debut the next day in a 4-3 loss against the New York Islanders. On October 28, 2013, Megna recorded his first NHL point on a Tanner Glass goal and also scored his first NHL goal in a 3-1 win against the Carolina Hurricanes. On July 10, 2014, the Penguins re-signed Megna to a one-year, two-way contract.
Jaylen Marselles Brown (born October 24, 1996) is a National Basketball Association player. He currently plays on the Boston Celtics. Brown was drafted in 2016 with the 3rd pick.

Dame Jayne Torvill (born 7 October 1957) is a British professional ice dancer and former competitor. Along with her long-term skating partner, Christopher Dean, she is considered one of the greatest ice dancers of all time. The pair won a gold at the 1984 Winter Olympics and won bronze at the 1994 Winter Olympics, becoming one of the oldest figure skating Olympic medalists.
Euclydes Barbosa, also known as Jaú (; December 7, 1909, São Paulo – February 26, 1988) was an association footballer who played in the central defender position.

Jean-Alain Boumsong Somkong (born 14 December 1979) is a French former professional footballer who played as a defender. He began his career with French club Le Havre in 1997 before joining AJ Auxerre in 2000. His performances at Auxerre earned him a move to Rangers in 2004. He moved to Newcastle United in 2005. where he spent two seasons. In 2006, he joined Juventus. He returned to France with Lyon in 2008. His last club was Greek Super League side Panathinaikos. Between 2003 and 2009, he made 27 appearances scoring 1 goal for the France national team. Score and result list France's goal tally first, score column indicates score after Boumsong goal.

Carlene Denise Moore-Begnaud (born August 27, 1973) is an American professional wrestler and manager. She is better known by her ring name Jazz. She is signed to WWE as a Performance Center trainer and is best known for wrestling there in the 2000s. She was a two-time WWE Women's Champion. She is also known for her time in Extreme Championship Wrestling (ECW), Impact Wrestling, and the National Wrestling Alliance, where she held the NWA World Women's Championship for over 900 days. She retired as a wrestler after Impact. She is married to Rodney Begnaud. He wrestled in WWE under the ring name Rodney Mack. Jean-Claude Henri Schindelholz (born 11 October 1940) is a Swiss former footballer. He played as a striker. At club level, he played for FC Moutier, Servette FC (1963–1971) and Vevey-Sports (1971–1973). He also played for the Switzerland national team. He played one game for Switzerland at the 1966 FIFA World Cup. Schindelholz was born in Courrendlin.

Jean-Claude Bouttier (13 October 1944 – 3 August 2019) was a French actor and professional boxer. During his boxing career, which spanned from 1965 to 1974, he won 64 out of 72 bouts, 43 of them by knockout. In June 1971 he won the European Boxing Union (EBU) middleweight title, and in 1972 and 1973 unsuccessfully was part of the WBC and WBA titles against Carlos Monzon. He lost the EBU title to Kevin Finnegan in May 1974.
Jean-Claude Annaert (22 August 1935 – 12 September 2020) was a racing cyclist from France. He was born on 22 August 1935 and died on 12 September 2020. Annaert rode in the 1957 Tour de France.
Jean-Claude Grèt was a racing cyclist from Switzerland. He was born on 21 October 1930 and died on 10 July 2001. Grèt became the Swiss National Road Race champion in 1958.

Jean-François "J.F." Labbé, nicknamed Ti-Mine, (born June 15, 1972) is aCanadian former professional ice hockey goaltender. After playing four seasons in the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League, Labbé began a very successful American Hockey League career. He played for the Prince Edward Island Senators, Cornwall Aces, Hershey Bears, Hamilton Bulldogs, Hartford Wolf Pack and Syracuse Crunch in his AHL tenure. His best season came in 1996–1997 with the Hershey Bears, when he won both the Hap Holmes Memorial Award for lowest goals against average and the Les Cunningham Award for league MVP. Labbé won the Calder Cup with the Hartford Wolf Pack in 2000. Labbé appeared in 15 NHL games: one with the New York Rangers at the end of the 1999–2000 season and 14 with the Columbus Blue Jackets during the 2001–02 and 2002–03 seasons. He played for the Saint-Georges Garaga in the Ligue Nord-Américaine de Hockey in 2003–2004 after a short stint with the Tolyatti Lada in the Russian Hockey Super League. Labbé has played in the DEL for three seasons, with Augsburger Panther in 2004–05 and with the Sinupret Ice Tigers in 2005–06 and 2006–07. For the 2007–08 season he joined the Vienna Capitals in Austria's Erste Bank Hockey League. Labbé was selected for induction as part of the American Hockey League Hall of Fame's 2016 class. 1996-97 AHL Hap Holmes Memorial Award (lowest GAA) 1999-00 AHL Hap Holmes Memorial Award (lowest GAA) Labbé currently holds records with the Syracuse Crunch for: Lowest GAA in a single season - 2.18 (2001–02) Highest single season save percentage -.928 (2001–02)

Jean-François "J. F." Jacques (born April 29, 1985) is a Canadian professional ice hockey left winger. He plays for the EC KAC of the Austrian Hockey League (EBEL). He has also played in the National Hockey League (NHL) with the Edmonton Oilers and the Anaheim Ducks. He was drafted by the Edmonton Oilers with the 68th pick in the 2003, NHL Entry Draft. He has played in the NHL for the Edmonton Oilers for 5 seasons. In the 2011-2012 season, he played for the Anaheim Ducks. In July 2012, he was signed to the Florida Panthers.

Jean-François Beltramini (5 February 1948 – 27 August 2014) was a French footballer. He played as a striker. He played professionally between 1969 and 1985. He played for clubs including Paris Saint-Germain, Stade de Reims, Paris and FC Rouen. Beltramini was born in Les Clayes-sous-Bois, Yvelines. He was of Italian ancestry. Beltramini died after a long illness on 27 August 2014 in Rouen, aged 66.

Jean-Jacques Marcel (13 June 1931 – 3 October 2014) was a French footballer. He played at the World Cup tournaments in 1954 and 1958. On 3 October 2014, it was announced by his former football club that Marcel died. He was 83.

Jean-François Joseph "J.F." Jomphe (born December 28, 1972) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey centre. He played parts of 5 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim, Phoenix Coyotes, and Montreal Canadiens. Outside of the NHL, Jomphe also played for the Krefeld Pinguine, Adler Mannheim, and ERC Ingolstadt of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL), and EHC Biel of the National League B (NLB). Before playing in the NHL, Jomphe played parts of three seasons with the Shawinigan Cataractes and one season with the Sherbrooke Faucons of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He was not drafted by an NHL team. He played one season with the San Diego Gulls of the International Hockey League and one season with the Greensboro Monarchs of the ECHL. He joined the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim during the 1995–96 season. On February 4, 1996, Jomphe made his NHL debut in a 4–1 loss against the Chicago Blackhawks. On February 10, he recorded his first two NHL points, assisting on goals by Jim Campbell and Jason York in a 4–1 loss against the New York Islanders. On February 14, Jomphe scored his first NHL goal against Curtis Joseph in a 4–1 loss against the Edmonton Oilers. On June 18, 1998, the Mighty Ducks traded Jomphe to the Phoenix Coyotes in exchange for Jim McKenzie. He played a total of 1 game for the Coyotes. On March 23, 1999, the Coyotes traded Jomphe to the Montreal Canadiens in exchange for cash. He played a total of 3 games for the Canadiens before they sent him down to play for their AHL-affiliate Fredericton Canadiens. After his NHL career was finished, played in Europe for a few years before retiring from playing professional ice hockey in 2005.

Jean-Gabriel Pageau (born November 11, 1992) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the New York Islanders of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Ottawa Senators. Before playing in the NHL, Pageau played three seasons with the Gatineau Olympiques and one season with the Chicoutimi Saguenéens of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He was drafted 96th overall by the Ottawa Senators of the 2011 NHL entry draft. On June 6, 2012, Pageau signed a three-year, $1.84 million entry-level contract to join the Senators. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Binghamton Senators. On April 11, 2013, Ottawa called him up and Pageau made his NHL debut in a 3–1 win against the Philadelphia Flyers. During the third period, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Daniel Alfredsson goal. The next day on April 12, Pageau scored his first NHL goal against Martin Brodeur in a 2–0 win against the New Jersey Devils. During game 3 of the Eastern conference quarter-finals on May 5, 2013, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 6–1 win against the Montreal Canadiens. On June 18, 2015, Pageau signed a two-year, $1.8 million contract to stay with the Senators. On July 17, 2017, Pageau signed a three-year, $9.3 million contract to stay with the Senators. On October 30, the league named him as the Third Star of the Week. On March 21, 2019, the league suspended Pageau for a regular season game and fined him $16,666.67 for illegally boarding Vancouver Canucks player Ashton Sautner. On February 24, 2020, the Senators traded Pageau to the New York Islanders in exchange for a 2020 conditional first-round draft pick, 2020 second-round draft pick, and a 2022 conditional third-round draft pick. That same day, Pageau signed a six-year, $30 million contract to stay with the Islanders. On March 6, 2026, Pageau signed a three-year, $14.55 million contract to stay with the Islanders.

Jean-Luc Bilodeau (born November 4, 1990) is a Canadian actor. He has been acting since 2004. He is best known for his role as Josh Trager in the ABC Family channel program Kyle XY. Bilodeau also appeared in many movies and television shows. These include, Ill Fated, Trick 'r Treat, 16 Wishes, No Ordinary Family and Best Player. He appeared in Emmalyn Estrada's music video "Don't Make Me Let You Go". He played Jeremy in the movie LOL. He currently stars in the ABC Family sitcom, Baby Daddy.

Jean-Michel Liade Gnonka (born July 20, 1980 in Ouagadougou) is a former Burkinabé football player. He played for 18 years and was part of the squads which took part in the African Cup of Nations tournaments of 1998, 2000, and 2004.

Jean-Louis Gasset (9 December 1953 – 26 December 2025) was a French footballer and manager. As a footballer, he played as a midfielder, spending ten years playing for his hometown club Montpellier. As a manager, he coached Montpellier (where he won the 1999 UEFA Intertoto Cup), Caen, Istres, Saint-Étienne, Bordeaux, the Ivory Coast, and Marseille. He also worked as an assistant manager under Luis Fernández at Paris Saint-Germain and Espanyol, and under Laurent Blanc at Bordeaux, France and Paris Saint-Germain. While manager of the Ivory Coast, he managed the team at the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations. He resigned from the job on 24 January 2024, after a poor performance in the group stages, and was replaced by Emerse Faé, who helped the Ivory Coast win the tournament. Gasset died on 26 December 2025, at the age of 72.

Jean-Pierre "J. P." Dumont (born April 1, 1978) is a Canadian retired professional ice hockey right winger. Dumont played 12 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played with the Chicago Blackhawks, Buffalo Sabres, and Nashville Predators. He also played for SC Bern of the National League A (NLA). Before playing in the NHL, Dumont played 4 seasons with the Val-d'Or Foreurs of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He was drafted with the 3rd overall pick by the New York Islanders in the 1996 NHL Entry Draft. Dumont had a contract dispute with the Islanders and they traded him and a 5th round draft pick to the Chicago Blackhawks for Dmitri Nabokov in 1998. Dumont played 72 games over two seasons with the Blackhawks and in March 2000, he was traded along with Doug Gilmour and a draft pick to the Buffalo Sabres for Michal Grosek. Dumont played 5 seasons with the Sabres and was named their captain in January 2004. After the Sabres rejected Dumont's $2.9-million arbitration award, he signed a two-year, $4.5-million contract with the Nashville Predators on August 29, 2006. On June 30, 2011, the Predators bought out Dumont's contract and he became an unrestricted free agent for July 1. He retired from playing professional ice hockey in 2013. Since retiring, Dumont is currently a member of tag HC Nashville which is based in Nashville, Tennessee.

Jean-Pierre Adams (10 March 1948 – 6 September 2021) was a French footballer. He played as a central defender. Adams started playing with RC Fontainebleau in 1967 as a striker, with whom he won the Championnat de France amateur twice. In 1970, he signed a contract with Nîmes Olympique, going on to remain in Ligue 1 for the following nine seasons, also representing in the competition OGC Nice and Paris Saint-Germain FC. In the 1971–72 campaign, Adams contributed with four goals in all 38 games to help Nîmes to a best-ever second place, also winning the Cup of the Alps. He added a career-best nine in 1973–74, for a final ninth position. On 15 June 1972, Adams made his debut for the French national team in an unofficial exhibition game against an African XI selected by the Confederation of African Football. On 17 March 1982, he slipped into a coma following problems caused by a knee operation in Nîmes. The surgery was to fix a torn knee tendon. He had suffered from oxygen loss in the brain after the anesthesiologist made a mistake. Adams died on 6 September 2021 at the age of 73, after being in a coma for almost 40 years.

Jean-Pierre Jaussaud (3 June 1937 – 21 July 2021) was a French racing driver. He was known for winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1978 and 1980. Jaussaud was born in Caen, France. He raced with Formula Three cars. Jaussaud died on 21 July 2021 in Caen of a heart attack, aged 84.
Jean-Pierre Kress was a footballer from France. He was born on 1 March 1930 and died on 22 April 2021. Kress played for the France national team in 1953.
